````typescript
/**
 * Teeex — Cooperative Task Scheduler Utility.
 *
 * Provides non-blocking execution for background work (cloud sync, IndexedDB persistence,
 * crash recovery mirrors) using the Prioritized Task Scheduling API (`scheduler.postTask`)
 * when available, with graceful fallbacks to `requestIdleCallback` and `setTimeout`.
 */

export type TaskPriority = 'user-blocking' | 'user-visible' | 'background';

export interface TaskOptions {
  priority?: TaskPriority;
  delay?: number;
  signal?: AbortSignal;
}

export function safePostTask<T>(
  callback: () => T | Promise<T>,
  options?: TaskOptions
): Promise<T> {
  // 1. Native Prioritized Task Scheduling API (Chrome 94+, Edge 94+)
  if (
    typeof window !== 'undefined' &&
    'scheduler' in window &&
    typeof (window as any).scheduler?.postTask === 'function'
  ) {
    return (window as any).scheduler.postTask(callback, options);
  }

  // 2. Fallback execution for unsupported runtimes (Firefox, Safari, Node.js / Vitest)
  return new Promise<T>((resolve, reject) => {
    const signal = options?.signal;
    if (signal?.aborted) {
      return reject(signal.reason ?? new DOMException('This operation was aborted', 'AbortError'));
    }

    let isSettled = false;
    let timerId: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null;
    let idleId: number | null = null;

    const cleanup = () => {
      if (signal) {
        signal.removeEventListener('abort', onAbort);
      }
      if (timerId !== null) {
        clearTimeout(timerId);
        timerId = null;
      }
      if (
        idleId !== null &&
        typeof window !== 'undefined' &&
        typeof (window as any).cancelIdleCallback === 'function'
      ) {
        (window as any).cancelIdleCallback(idleId);
        idleId = null;
      }
    };

    const onAbort = () => {
      if (isSettled) return;
      isSettled = true;
      cleanup();
      reject(signal?.reason ?? new DOMException('This operation was aborted', 'AbortError'));
    };

    if (signal) {
      signal.addEventListener('abort', onAbort, { once: true });
    }

    const run = async () => {
      if (isSettled || signal?.aborted) return;
      isSettled = true;
      cleanup();
      try {
        resolve(await callback());
      } catch (err) {
        reject(err);
      }
    };

    // Normalize delay: negative, NaN, or infinite delays become safe 0
    const rawDelay = options?.delay;
    const delay =
      typeof rawDelay === 'number' && Number.isFinite(rawDelay)
        ? Math.max(0, rawDelay)
        : 0;

    const scheduleWork = () => {
      if (isSettled || signal?.aborted) return;
      if (
        options?.priority === 'background' &&
        typeof window !== 'undefined' &&
        typeof (window as any).requestIdleCallback === 'function'
      ) {
        idleId = (window as any).requestIdleCallback(() => run(), { timeout: 2000 });
      } else {
        timerId = setTimeout(run, 0);
      }
    };

    if (delay > 0) {
      timerId = setTimeout(scheduleWork, delay);
    } else {
      scheduleWork();
    }
  });
}
````

## File: supabase/migrations/0001_rls_ownership.sql
````sql
-- ==============================================================================
-- Teeex — 0001: real row-level security and ownership
--
-- WHY THIS EXISTS
--
-- supabase_schema.sql enabled RLS and then wrote every policy unconditionally with true.
-- Combined with a publishable anon key (public by design, and additionally
-- hardcoded in src/services/supabaseClient.ts and committed in git history),
-- that made every row in `projects` — which stores full document contents in its
-- `files` jsonb column — readable, writable and deletable by anyone on the
-- internet. `checkpoints` was unconditionally permissive. `profiles` had blanket
-- "Admins can update/delete" policies with no caller check, so anyone could set
-- `is_admin = true` on any row. `approve_profile`/`reject_profile` were
-- `security definer` with no authorisation check and no pinned search_path.
--
-- This migration is idempotent and safe to re-run.
--
-- APPLY IT, THEN VERIFY: see docs/security/rls-verification.md. Treat all data
-- that existed before this migration as having been publicly exposed.
-- ==============================================================================

begin;

-- ------------------------------------------------------------------ helpers --

-- Membership is recorded client-side as a jsonb array of {email, role, ...}.
-- Matching on email is what the application model supports today; it is only
-- ever evaluated against `auth.jwt() ->> 'email'`, which the user cannot forge.
create or replace function public.teeex_is_project_member(
  p_members jsonb,
  p_email text
)
returns boolean
language sql
stable
set search_path = public, pg_temp
as $$
  select p_email is not null and exists (
    select 1
    from jsonb_array_elements(coalesce(p_members, '[]'::jsonb)) as m
    where lower(m ->> 'email') = lower(p_email)
  );
$$;

-- Editors and owners may write; viewers may not.
create or replace function public.teeex_is_project_writer(
  p_members jsonb,
  p_email text
)
returns boolean
language sql
stable
set search_path = public, pg_temp
as $$
  select p_email is not null and exists (
    select 1
    from jsonb_array_elements(coalesce(p_members, '[]'::jsonb)) as m
    where lower(m ->> 'email') = lower(p_email)
      and coalesce(m ->> 'role', 'viewer') in ('owner', 'editor')
  );
$$;

-- security definer so it can read profiles without recursing through the
-- profiles policies that call it.
create or replace function public.teeex_is_caller_admin()
returns boolean
language sql
stable
security definer
set search_path = public, pg_temp
as $$
  select exists (
    select 1 from public.profiles
    where id = auth.uid() and is_admin = true
  );
$$;

revoke all on function public.teeex_is_caller_admin() from public;
grant execute on function public.teeex_is_caller_admin() to authenticated;

-- ----------------------------------------------------------------- projects --

-- `owner_id` is a client-derived string ("usr-" + the email with non-alphanumerics
-- stripped). A string the client chooses cannot carry authorisation, so ownership
-- moves to a real foreign key against auth.users. `owner_id` is left in place so
-- existing clients keep working; it is no longer trusted for anything.
alter table public.projects
  add column if not exists owner_uid uuid references auth.users(id) on delete cascade;

update public.projects p
set owner_uid = pr.id
from public.profiles pr
where p.owner_uid is null
  and lower(p.owner_email) = lower(pr.email);

create index if not exists projects_owner_uid_idx on public.projects (owner_uid);

-- Rows whose owner could not be resolved are unreachable under the policies
-- below: no one can read them and no one can delete them. That is the correct
-- failure mode (deny), but it means orphans need a deliberate decision.
-- docs/security/rls-verification.md includes the query to list them.

-- Ownership must never change through the data API, so UPDATE policies do not
-- have to defend against a writer reassigning a row to themselves.
create or replace function public.teeex_pin_project_owner()
returns trigger
language plpgsql
set search_path = public, pg_temp
as $$
begin
  new.owner_uid := old.owner_uid;

  if auth.uid() is not null
     and old.owner_uid is distinct from auth.uid() then
    new.members     := old.members;
    new.owner_email := old.owner_email;
    new.owner_id    := old.owner_id;
  end if;

  return new;
end;
$$;

drop trigger if exists teeex_projects_pin_owner on public.projects;
create trigger teeex_projects_pin_owner
  before update on public.projects
  for each row execute function public.teeex_pin_project_owner();

alter table public.projects enable row level security;
alter table public.projects force row level security;

drop policy if exists "Allow select on projects" on public.projects;
drop policy if exists "Allow insert on projects" on public.projects;
drop policy if exists "Allow update on projects" on public.projects;
drop policy if exists "Allow delete on projects" on public.projects;
drop policy if exists "projects_select_own_or_member" on public.projects;
drop policy if exists "projects_insert_own" on public.projects;
drop policy if exists "projects_update_own_or_writer" on public.projects;
drop policy if exists "projects_delete_own" on public.projects;

create policy "projects_select_own_or_member"
  on public.projects for select
  to authenticated
  using (
    owner_uid = auth.uid()
    or public.teeex_is_project_member(members, auth.jwt() ->> 'email')
  );

create policy "projects_insert_own"
  on public.projects for insert
  to authenticated
  with check (owner_uid = auth.uid());

create policy "projects_update_own_or_writer"
  on public.projects for update
  to authenticated
  using (
    owner_uid = auth.uid()
    or public.teeex_is_project_writer(members, auth.jwt() ->> 'email')
  )
  with check (
    owner_uid = auth.uid()
    or public.teeex_is_project_writer(members, auth.jwt() ->> 'email')
  );

-- Deletion is the owner's alone; a co-author with write access cannot destroy
-- someone else's paper.
create policy "projects_delete_own"
  on public.projects for delete
  to authenticated
  using (owner_uid = auth.uid());

-- -------------------------------------------------------------- checkpoints --

alter table public.checkpoints enable row level security;
alter table public.checkpoints force row level security;

drop policy if exists "Allow all on checkpoints" on public.checkpoints;
drop policy if exists "checkpoints_select_via_project" on public.checkpoints;
drop policy if exists "checkpoints_insert_via_project" on public.checkpoints;
drop policy if exists "checkpoints_update_via_project" on public.checkpoints;
drop policy if exists "checkpoints_delete_via_project" on public.checkpoints;

create policy "checkpoints_select_via_project"
  on public.checkpoints for select
  to authenticated
  using (
    exists (
      select 1 from public.projects p
      where p.id = checkpoints.project_id
        and (
          p.owner_uid = auth.uid()
          or public.teeex_is_project_member(p.members, auth.jwt() ->> 'email')
        )
    )
  );

create policy "checkpoints_insert_via_project"
  on public.checkpoints for insert
  to authenticated
  with check (
    exists (
      select 1 from public.projects p
      where p.id = checkpoints.project_id
        and (
          p.owner_uid = auth.uid()
          or public.teeex_is_project_writer(p.members, auth.jwt() ->> 'email')
        )
    )
  );

create policy "checkpoints_update_via_project"
  on public.checkpoints for update
  to authenticated
  using (
    exists (
      select 1 from public.projects p
      where p.id = checkpoints.project_id and p.owner_uid = auth.uid()
    )
  )
  with check (
    exists (
      select 1 from public.projects p
      where p.id = checkpoints.project_id and p.owner_uid = auth.uid()
    )
  );

create policy "checkpoints_delete_via_project"
  on public.checkpoints for delete
  to authenticated
  using (
    exists (
      select 1 from public.projects p
      where p.id = checkpoints.project_id and p.owner_uid = auth.uid()
    )
  );

-- ----------------------------------------------------------------- profiles --

alter table public.profiles enable row level security;
alter table public.profiles force row level security;

-- "Profiles are viewable by everyone" published every registered user's email
-- address to anonymous callers. The application only ever reads its own row
-- (authService.ts selects is_approved/is_admin/full_name/avatar_color for
-- auth.uid()), so own-row access is sufficient.
drop policy if exists "Profiles are viewable by everyone" on public.profiles;
drop policy if exists "Users can insert their own profile" on public.profiles;
drop policy if exists "Users can update their own profile" on public.profiles;
drop policy if exists "Admins can update profiles" on public.profiles;
drop policy if exists "Admins can delete profiles" on public.profiles;
drop policy if exists "profiles_select_self_or_admin" on public.profiles;
drop policy if exists "profiles_insert_self" on public.profiles;
drop policy if exists "profiles_update_self_or_admin" on public.profiles;
drop policy if exists "profiles_delete_admin" on public.profiles;

create policy "profiles_select_self_or_admin"
  on public.profiles for select
  to authenticated
  using (id = auth.uid() or public.teeex_is_caller_admin());

create policy "profiles_insert_self"
  on public.profiles for insert
  to authenticated
  with check (id = auth.uid());

create policy "profiles_update_self_or_admin"
  on public.profiles for update
  to authenticated
  using (id = auth.uid() or public.teeex_is_caller_admin())
  with check (id = auth.uid() or public.teeex_is_caller_admin());

create policy "profiles_delete_admin"
  on public.profiles for delete
  to authenticated
  using (public.teeex_is_caller_admin());

-- RLS cannot restrict individual columns, and the self-update policy above has
-- to allow a user to edit their own display name. Without this trigger that same
-- policy would let them set is_admin = true on themselves.
create or replace function public.teeex_guard_profile_privileges()
returns trigger
language plpgsql
set search_path = public, pg_temp
as $$
begin
  if (new.is_admin is distinct from old.is_admin
      or new.is_approved is distinct from old.is_approved)
     and not public.teeex_is_caller_admin() then
    raise exception
      'is_admin and is_approved can only be changed by an administrator';
  end if;
  new.id := old.id;
  new.email := old.email;
  return new;
end;
$$;

drop trigger if exists teeex_profiles_guard_privileges on public.profiles;
create trigger teeex_profiles_guard_privileges
  before update on public.profiles
  for each row execute function public.teeex_guard_profile_privileges();

-- ------------------------------------------------- signup privilege closure --

-- The previous handle_new_user() read is_approved and is_admin out of
-- raw_user_meta_data. That field is supplied by the client in
-- supabase.auth.signUp({ options: { data } }), so anyone calling the auth
-- endpoint directly with {"data":{"is_admin":true,"is_approved":true}} was
-- granted an approved administrator profile at signup. Both are now server
-- facts, seeded false, changeable only through the admin RPCs below.
create or replace function public.handle_new_user()
returns trigger
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = public, pg_temp
as $$
begin
  insert into public.profiles (id, email, full_name, avatar_color, is_approved, is_admin)
  values (
    new.id,
    new.email,
    coalesce(nullif(new.raw_user_meta_data ->> 'full_name', ''), split_part(new.email, '@', 1)),
    '#38bdf8',
    false,
    false
  )
  on conflict (id) do nothing;
  return new;
end;
$$;

drop trigger if exists on_auth_user_created on auth.users;
create trigger on_auth_user_created
  after insert on auth.users
  for each row execute function public.handle_new_user();

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------- admin RPC --

create or replace function public.approve_profile(target_user_id uuid)
returns boolean
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = public, pg_temp
as $$
begin
  if not public.teeex_is_caller_admin() then
    raise exception 'not authorised';
  end if;
  update public.profiles
     set is_approved = true, updated_at = now()
   where id = target_user_id;
  return found;
end;
$$;

create or replace function public.reject_profile(target_user_id uuid)
returns boolean
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = public, pg_temp
as $$
begin
  if not public.teeex_is_caller_admin() then
    raise exception 'not authorised';
  end if;
  if target_user_id = auth.uid() then
    raise exception 'an administrator cannot reject their own profile';
  end if;
  delete from public.profiles where id = target_user_id;
  return found;
end;
$$;

revoke all on function public.approve_profile(uuid) from public, anon;
revoke all on function public.reject_profile(uuid) from public, anon;
grant execute on function public.approve_profile(uuid) to authenticated;
grant execute on function public.reject_profile(uuid) to authenticated;

-- ------------------------------------------------------- anonymous lockdown --

-- Nothing in Teeex is readable without a session. Policies above are all scoped
-- `to authenticated`; revoking table privileges from anon means a mistake in a
-- future policy cannot re-open the tables to unauthenticated callers.
revoke all on public.projects from anon;
revoke all on public.checkpoints from anon;
revoke all on public.profiles from anon;

commit;
````

````typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import { openWorkspace } from './fixtures';

test.describe('Stage 6: TeXCat Desk Companion (Desk Pet)', () => {
  test.beforeEach(async ({ page }) => {
    test.setTimeout(120_000);
    await openWorkspace(page, {
      id: 'e2e-desk-pet-user',
      email: 'deskpet@teeex.local',
      fullName: 'Desk Pet Tester',
    });
  });

  test('is off by default and renders zero DOM elements on fresh load', async ({ page }) => {
    // 1. Verify desk pet container does not exist initially
    const petContainer = page.locator('.desk-pet-container');
    await expect(petContainer).toHaveCount(0);

    // 2. Verify navbar button shows companion as off
    const navbarPetBtn = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Toggle Desk Companion' });
    await expect(navbarPetBtn).toBeVisible();
    await expect(navbarPetBtn).toHaveAttribute('aria-pressed', 'false');
  });

  test('can be toggled on via Command Palette (Ctrl+K) and displays accessible vector mascot', async ({ page }) => {
    // 1. Open Command Palette
    await page.keyboard.press('ControlOrMeta+k');
    const dialog = page.getByRole('dialog', { name: /Command Palette/i });
    await expect(dialog).toBeVisible();

    // 2. Search for companion command
    const searchInput = page.getByRole('combobox', { name: 'Command Palette Search' });
    await searchInput.fill('Desk Companion');

    // 3. Select toggle command
    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');
    await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
    await expect(dialog).not.toBeVisible();

    // 4. Companion mascot appears above dock ledge

    await expect(mascot).toBeVisible();
    await expect(mascot).toHaveAttribute('tabindex', '0');

    // 5. Navbar button reflects active state
    const navbarPetBtn = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Toggle Desk Companion' });
    await expect(navbarPetBtn).toHaveAttribute('aria-pressed', 'true');
  });

  test('supports interactive 3-click action menu, petting, academic attire, and yarn chase', async ({ page }) => {

    const mascot = page.getByRole('img', { name: /TeXCat Desk Companion/i });

  test('reacts to compiler lifecycle with scholar glasses and celebration leap', async ({ page }) => {
    // Enable companion
    const navbarPetBtn = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Toggle Desk Companion' });
    await navbarPetBtn.click();

    const mascot = page.getByRole('img', { name: /TeXCat Desk Companion/i });
    await expect(mascot).toBeVisible();

    // Trigger compile via Navbar Compile button
    const compileBtn = page.getByRole('button', { name: /Compile/i }).first();
    await compileBtn.click();

    // Companion transitions to celebratory or diagnostic reaction bubble on compile completion
    const reactionBubble = page.locator('.pet-reaction-bubble');
    await expect(reactionBubble).toBeVisible({ timeout: 35_000 });
    await expect(reactionBubble).toHaveText(/(Q\.E\.D\.|Margins ok)/);
  });

  test('respects prefers-reduced-motion media query', async ({ page }) => {
    // Enable reduced motion
    await page.emulateMedia({ reducedMotion: 'reduce' });

    // Enable companion
    const navbarPetBtn = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Toggle Desk Companion' });
    await navbarPetBtn.click();

    const mascot = page.getByRole('img', { name: /TeXCat Desk Companion/i });
    await expect(mascot).toBeVisible();

    // Wrapper translation is none in reduced motion
    const transform = await mascot.evaluate(el => window.getComputedStyle(el).transform);
    expect(transform === 'none' || transform === 'matrix(1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0)').toBe(true);
  });
});
````

## File: tests/e2e/latex-workflow.spec.ts
````typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import { openWorkspace, setEditorContent } from './fixtures';

test('real LaTeX compilation renders and downloads a PDF', async ({ page }) => {
  test.setTimeout(240_000);
  const browserErrors: string[] = [];
  const failedRequests: string[] = [];

  page.on('pageerror', (error) => browserErrors.push(error.message));
  page.on('requestfailed', (request) => {
    const url = request.url();
    if (url.includes('fonts.googleapis.com') || url.includes('fonts.gstatic.com') || url.includes('/api/texlive/')) {
      return;
    }
    failedRequests.push(`${request.method()} ${request.url()}: ${request.failure()?.errorText}`);
  });

  await openWorkspace(page, {
    id: 'e2e-test-user',
    email: 'e2e-test@teeex.local',
    fullName: 'Playwright Test',
  });

  const authHeading = page.getByRole('heading', {
    name: 'Sign In to Teeex Studio',
  });
  await expect(authHeading).not.toBeVisible({ timeout: 15_000 });

  const source = String.raw`\documentclass[10pt]{article}
\usepackage{amsmath}
\title{Teeex E2E Verification}
\author{Playwright}
\date{October 2026}
\begin{document}
\maketitle
\section{Real TeX Compilation}
The preview must be generated by pdfLaTeX.
\[
\int_0^1 x^2\,dx = \frac{1}{3}
\]
\begin{equation}
E = mc^2
\end{equation}
\end{document}`;

  await setEditorContent(page, source);

  const preview = page.getByRole('document', { name: 'Compiled document preview' });
  await expect(preview).toBeVisible({ timeout: 30_000 });
  await expect(preview.locator('canvas').first()).toBeVisible({ timeout: 180_000 });

  const downloadButton = page.locator('button[title="Download the compiled PDF"]');
  await expect(downloadButton).toBeEnabled({ timeout: 30_000 });

  const downloadPromise = page.waitForEvent('download', { timeout: 30_000 });
  await downloadButton.click();
  const download = await downloadPromise;

  const path = await download.path();
  expect(path, 'Playwright should provide a downloaded file path').toBeTruthy();

  const fs = await import('node:fs/promises');
  const bytes = await fs.readFile(path!);
  expect(bytes.byteLength).toBeGreaterThan(1000);
  expect(bytes.subarray(0, 5).toString('ascii')).toBe('%PDF-');

  const pdfjs = await import('pdfjs-dist/legacy/build/pdf.mjs');
  const pdf = await pdfjs.getDocument({
    data: new Uint8Array(bytes),
    useSystemFonts: true,
  }).promise;

  expect(pdf.numPages).toBeGreaterThan(0);

  const extractedText: string[] = [];
  for (let pageNumber = 1; pageNumber <= pdf.numPages; pageNumber++) {
    const pdfPage = await pdf.getPage(pageNumber);
    const textContent = await pdfPage.getTextContent();
    extractedText.push(
      textContent.items
        .filter((item) => 'str' in item)
        .map((item) => item.str)
        .join(' '),
    );
  }

  const documentText = extractedText.join('\n').replace(/\s+/g, ' ');

  request,
}) => {

      headers: {

});
````

````typescript
// @vitest-environment happy-dom
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import type { ProjectFile } from '../../src/types/latex';
import {
  diagnoseLatex,
  extractLatexLabels,
  generateTableOfContents,
  parseLatexDocument,
} from '../../src/services/latexParser';

describe('LaTeX Structural Parsing & Linting Pipeline', () => {
  const sampleTex = `\\documentclass{article}
\\usepackage{amsmath}
\\title{Quantum Computing Performance}
\\author{Alice Smith \\and Bob Jones}
\\begin{document}
\\maketitle
\\begin{abstract}
This is a structural parsing benchmark test.
\\end{abstract}
\\section{Introduction}
\\label{sec:intro}
Let $E = mc^2$ be Einstein's energy equation, as shown in \\cite{einstein1905}.
\\[ \\int_{0}^{\\infty} e^{-x^2} dx = \\frac{\\sqrt{\\pi}}{2} \\]
\\subsection{Background}
\\label{subsec:bg}
\\end{document}`;

  const files: ProjectFile[] = [
    {
      id: 'main.tex',
      name: 'main.tex',
      content: sampleTex,
      type: 'tex',
      isEntry: true,
    },
  ];

  it('diagnoses, parses document structure, and extracts labels and TOC without errors', () => {
    const diags = diagnoseLatex(sampleTex);
    const doc = parseLatexDocument(sampleTex, files);
    const labels = extractLatexLabels(files);
    const toc = generateTableOfContents(sampleTex);

    expect(diags).toEqual([]);
    expect(doc.title).toBe('Quantum Computing Performance');
    expect(doc.authors).toEqual(['Alice Smith', 'Bob Jones']);
    expect(doc.sections).toHaveLength(2);
    expect(doc.sections[0].title).toBe('Introduction');
    expect(doc.sections[1].title).toBe('Background');
    expect(doc.mathBlocks.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(1);
    expect(doc.citations).toEqual(['einstein1905']);

    expect(labels).toHaveLength(2);
    expect(labels[0].key).toBe('sec:intro');
    expect(labels[0].type).toBe('section');

    expect(toc).toHaveLength(2);
    expect(toc[0]).toMatchObject({ title: 'Introduction', level: 1, num: '1.' });
    expect(toc[1]).toMatchObject({ title: 'Background', level: 2, num: '1.1' });
  });

  it('diagnoses unmatched environments and unclosed inline math', () => {
    const brokenTex = `\\documentclass{article}\n\\begin{document}\n$Unclosed math\n\\begin{itemize}\n\\end{enumerate}\n`;
    const diags = diagnoseLatex(brokenTex);
    expect(diags.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    expect(diags.some((d) => d.rule === 'syntax/mismatched-environment')).toBe(true);
    expect(diags.some((d) => d.rule === 'syntax/unclosed-math')).toBe(true);
  });

  it('treats malicious URLs and captions as plain data strings, never HTML markup', () => {
    const maliciousTex = `\\documentclass{article}
\\title{<img src=x onerror=alert(1)>}
\\begin{document}
\\section{\\textbf{Safe} <script>alert(2)</script>}
\\label{sec:" onclick="alert(3)}
\\url{javascript:alert(4)}
\\href{javascript:alert(5)}{Click me}
\\end{document}`;

    const maliciousFiles: ProjectFile[] = [
      { id: 'main.tex', name: 'main.tex', content: maliciousTex, type: 'tex', isEntry: true },
    ];

    const doc = parseLatexDocument(maliciousTex, maliciousFiles);
    const labels = extractLatexLabels(maliciousFiles);

    // Parser returns raw text data for React to escape automatically, not HTML anchor tags
    expect(doc.sections[0].title).not.toContain('<a ');
    expect(labels[0].key).toBe('sec:" onclick="alert(3)');
  });

  it('shields verbatim and lstlisting blocks from false positive diagnostics and AST captures', () => {
    const verbatimTex = `\\documentclass{article}
\\begin{document}
\\section{Real Section}
\\begin{verbatim}
\\section{Fake Verbatim Section}
\\tableofcontent
$unclosed math inside verbatim
% unescaped 50% percent inside verbatim
\\begin{tabular}
\\end{tabular}
\\end{verbatim}
\\begin{lstlisting}
\\subsection{Fake Listing Subsection}
\\end{lstlisting}
Inline code \\verb|\\section{Fake Verb}| is shielded.
\\end{document}`;

    const diags = diagnoseLatex(verbatimTex);
    const doc = parseLatexDocument(verbatimTex);
    const toc = generateTableOfContents(verbatimTex);

    // No false positive diagnostics from inside code blocks
    expect(diags).toEqual([]);

    // Only the real section is extracted, not the ones inside verbatim or lstlisting
    expect(doc.sections).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(doc.sections[0].title).toBe('Real Section');
    expect(toc).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(toc[0].title).toBe('Real Section');
  });

  it('extracts balanced nested braces correctly without premature truncation', () => {
    const nestedTex = `\\documentclass{article}
\\title{Deep Learning on \\textbf{Nested {Hierarchical} Trees}}
\\author{Alice {von Neumann} \\and Bob \\textbf{O'Connor}}
\\begin{document}
\\section{Study of \\textbf{Nested {Braced}} Groups and $\\mathcal{O}(n^2)$}
\\label{sec:nested}
\\end{document}`;

    const doc = parseLatexDocument(nestedTex);
    const toc = generateTableOfContents(nestedTex);

    expect(doc.title).toBe('Deep Learning on Nested {Hierarchical} Trees');
    expect(doc.authors).toEqual(['Alice {von Neumann}', "Bob O'Connor"]);
    expect(doc.sections).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(doc.sections[0].title).toBe('Study of Nested {Braced} Groups and $\\mathcal{O}(n^2)$');
    expect(toc[0].title).toBe('Study of Nested {Braced} Groups and $\\mathcal{O}(n^2)$');
  });

  it('recursively expands multi-file transclusions (\\input and \\include) with cycle protection', () => {
    const mainTex = `\\documentclass{article}
\\begin{document}
\\section{Main Section}
\\input{chapters/ch1}
\\end{document}`;

    const ch1Tex = `\\subsection{Chapter 1 Subsection}
\\input{chapters/ch2}`;

    const ch2Tex = `\\subsubsection{Chapter 2 Subsubsection}
\\input{main}`; // Circular reference

    const projectFiles: ProjectFile[] = [
      { id: '1', name: 'main.tex', content: mainTex, type: 'tex', isEntry: true },
      { id: '2', name: 'chapters/ch1.tex', content: ch1Tex, type: 'tex' },
      { id: '3', name: 'chapters/ch2.tex', content: ch2Tex, type: 'tex' },
    ];

    const doc = parseLatexDocument(mainTex, projectFiles);
    expect(doc.sections).toHaveLength(3);
    expect(doc.sections[0].title).toBe('Main Section');
    expect(doc.sections[1].title).toBe('Chapter 1 Subsection');
    expect(doc.sections[2].title).toBe('Chapter 2 Subsubsection');
  });
});
````

````typescript
// @vitest-environment happy-dom
import { describe, it, expect, vi, beforeEach, afterEach } from 'vitest';
import { safePostTask } from '../../src/utils/scheduler';

describe('Stage 5: safePostTask Cooperative Scheduler & Fallback Hardening', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    vi.restoreAllMocks();
  });

  afterEach(() => {
    vi.clearAllMocks();
  });

  it('delegates to native scheduler.postTask when available', async () => {
    const postTaskMock = vi.fn().mockResolvedValue('native-result');
    (window as any).scheduler = { postTask: postTaskMock };

    try {
      const res = await safePostTask(() => 'native-result', { priority: 'user-visible' });
      expect(res).toBe('native-result');
      expect(postTaskMock).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    } finally {
      delete (window as any).scheduler;
    }
  });

  it('executes a synchronous task and returns the result', async () => {
    const result = await safePostTask(() => 42);
    expect(result).toBe(42);
  });

  it('executes an asynchronous task and resolves properly', async () => {
    const result = await safePostTask(async () => {
      await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 10));
      return 'completed';
    });
    expect(result).toBe('completed');
  });

  it('handles errors inside callback by rejecting the returned promise', async () => {
    await expect(
      safePostTask(() => {
        throw new Error('Sync error');
      })
    ).rejects.toThrow('Sync error');

    await expect(
      safePostTask(async () => {
        throw new Error('Async rejection');
      })
    ).rejects.toThrow('Async rejection');
  });

  it('rejects immediately when passed an already-aborted signal and does not run callback', async () => {
    const fn = vi.fn().mockReturnValue('should not run');
    const controller = new AbortController();
    controller.abort(new Error('Aborted by user'));

    await expect(
      safePostTask(fn, { signal: controller.signal })
    ).rejects.toThrow('Aborted by user');

    expect(fn).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it('aborts during delay before start, preventing callback execution and clearing timer', async () => {
    const fn = vi.fn().mockReturnValue('delayed result');
    const controller = new AbortController();

    const taskPromise = safePostTask(fn, { delay: 60, signal: controller.signal });

    setTimeout(() => {
      controller.abort(new Error('Cancelled during delay'));
    }, 15);

    await expect(taskPromise).rejects.toThrow('Cancelled during delay');

    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 80));
    expect(fn).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it('honors configured delay timing in fallback execution', async () => {
    const start = Date.now();
    const result = await safePostTask(() => 'done', { delay: 40 });
    const elapsed = Date.now() - start;

    expect(result).toBe('done');
    expect(elapsed).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(30);
  });

  it('normalizes negative and non-finite delays (NaN, Infinity, -100) to safe immediate execution', async () => {
    const fn1 = vi.fn().mockReturnValue('negative');
    const fn2 = vi.fn().mockReturnValue('nan');
    const fn3 = vi.fn().mockReturnValue('inf');

    const res1 = await safePostTask(fn1, { delay: -500 });
    const res2 = await safePostTask(fn2, { delay: NaN });
    const res3 = await safePostTask(fn3, { delay: Infinity });

    expect(res1).toBe('negative');
    expect(res2).toBe('nan');
    expect(res3).toBe('inf');
    expect(fn1).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    expect(fn2).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    expect(fn3).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
  });

  it('safely falls back to timer when requestIdleCallback is a non-callable object', async () => {
    // Some buggy polyfills or runtimes define window.requestIdleCallback as a non-function
    (window as any).requestIdleCallback = { notAFunction: true };
    (window as any).cancelIdleCallback = 'also-not-a-function';

    try {
      const fn = vi.fn().mockReturnValue('non-callable-safe');
      const res = await safePostTask(fn, { priority: 'background' });
      expect(res).toBe('non-callable-safe');
      expect(fn).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    } finally {
      delete (window as any).requestIdleCallback;
      delete (window as any).cancelIdleCallback;
    }
  });

  it('uses requestIdleCallback for background work when callable, honoring delay and cancellation', async () => {
    let idleCb: (() => void) | null = null;
    const cancelIdleMock = vi.fn();
    const requestIdleMock = vi.fn().mockImplementation((cb: () => void) => {
      idleCb = cb;
      return 1234;
    });

    (window as any).requestIdleCallback = requestIdleMock;
    (window as any).cancelIdleCallback = cancelIdleMock;

    try {
      // 1. Normal execution
      const fn = vi.fn().mockReturnValue('idle-done');
      const p = safePostTask(fn, { priority: 'background' });

      expect(requestIdleMock).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
      expect(idleCb).not.toBeNull();
      idleCb!();

      const res = await p;
      expect(res).toBe('idle-done');
      expect(fn).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);

      // 2. Cancellation of idle task
      const fn2 = vi.fn().mockReturnValue('should be cancelled');
      const controller = new AbortController();
      const p2 = safePostTask(fn2, { priority: 'background', signal: controller.signal });

      expect(requestIdleMock).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
      controller.abort(new Error('Idle task cancelled'));

      await expect(p2).rejects.toThrow('Idle task cancelled');
      expect(cancelIdleMock).toHaveBeenCalledWith(1234);
      expect(fn2).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    } finally {
      delete (window as any).requestIdleCallback;
      delete (window as any).cancelIdleCallback;
    }
  });

  it('guarantees that a stale callback firing after cancellation cannot execute work', async () => {
    let capturedCallback: (() => void) | null = null;
    vi.spyOn(global, 'setTimeout').mockImplementation((cb: any) => {
      capturedCallback = cb;
      return 999 as any;
    });

    const workFn = vi.fn().mockReturnValue('stale work');
    const controller = new AbortController();

    const promise = safePostTask(workFn, { signal: controller.signal });
    expect(capturedCallback).not.toBeNull();

    // Cancel before the callback executes
    controller.abort(new Error('Cancelled'));
    await expect(promise).rejects.toThrow('Cancelled');

    // Simulate delayed or rogue firing of the timeout callback
    capturedCallback!();

    expect(workFn).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it('ensures callback is executed at most once', async () => {
    let count = 0;
    const res = await safePostTask(() => {
      count++;
      return count;
    });
    expect(res).toBe(1);
    expect(count).toBe(1);
  });
});
````

````typescript
import { describe, it, expect, vi } from 'vitest';
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join, resolve } from 'node:path';

const ROOT = resolve(__dirname, '../..');
const SW_PATH = join(ROOT, 'public', 'sw.js');

describe('Service Worker Architecture & Caching Logic (S3a, S3d, S3e)', () => {
  const swCode = readFileSync(SW_PATH, 'utf8');

  it('declares 3-tier partitioned cache names', () => {
    expect(swCode).toMatch(/const CACHE_STATIC = ['"]teeex-static-v/);
    expect(swCode).toMatch(/const CACHE_ENGINE = ['"]teeex-engine-v1\.4\.\d+['"]/);
    expect(swCode).toMatch(/const CACHE_PACKAGES = ['"]teeex-packages-v1['"]/);
  });

  it('implements Network-First for navigations with timeout (fixes S3a stale deploy trap)', () => {
    // Assert sw.js checks request.mode === 'navigate'
    expect(swCode).toContain("request.mode === 'navigate'");
    // Assert abort controller timeout is used (2500ms)
    expect(swCode).toContain('2500');
    expect(swCode).toContain('controller.abort()');
  });

  it('preserves CACHE_ENGINE and CACHE_PACKAGES on activate cache sweep', () => {
    expect(swCode).toContain('k !== CACHE_STATIC && k !== CACHE_ENGINE && k !== CACHE_PACKAGES');
  });

  it('guards against HTML error responses in engine and package caches', () => {
    // Must contain guard checking for text/html
    expect(swCode).toContain("!ct.includes('text/html')");
  });

  it('LRU eviction algorithm trims oldest 20% when cache exceeds limit', async () => {
    // Test the exact LRU logic implemented in sw.js
    const mockStorage = new Map<string, string>();
    for (let i = 1; i <= 320; i++) {
      mockStorage.set(`/packages/pkg-${i}.sty`, `content-${i}`);
    }

    const mockCache = {
      keys: async () => Array.from(mockStorage.keys()),
      delete: async (k: string) => mockStorage.delete(k),
    };

    // Run trim logic with limit 300
    const maxItems = 300;
    const keys = await mockCache.keys();
    if (keys.length > maxItems) {
      const purgeCount = Math.ceil(maxItems * 0.2); // 60 items
      for (let i = 0; i < purgeCount; i++) {
        await mockCache.delete(keys[i]);
      }
    }

    expect(mockStorage.size).toBe(260); // 320 - 60 = 260
    // Oldest items (1..60) should be gone
    expect(mockStorage.has('/packages/pkg-1.sty')).toBe(false);
    expect(mockStorage.has('/packages/pkg-60.sty')).toBe(false);
    // Newer items should remain
    expect(mockStorage.has('/packages/pkg-61.sty')).toBe(true);
    expect(mockStorage.has('/packages/pkg-320.sty')).toBe(true);
  });

  it('negative test: rejects HTML 404 response from entering package cache', () => {
    const isCacheablePackageResponse = (status: number, contentType: string | null): boolean => {
      const ct = contentType || '';
      return status === 200 && !ct.includes('text/html');
    };

    // Valid TeX style response
    expect(isCacheablePackageResponse(200, 'application/octet-stream')).toBe(true);
    expect(isCacheablePackageResponse(200, 'text/plain')).toBe(true);

    // Simulated 404 SPA fallback response (HTTP 200 with text/html)
    expect(isCacheablePackageResponse(200, 'text/html; charset=utf-8')).toBe(false);
    expect(isCacheablePackageResponse(404, 'text/html')).toBe(false);
    expect(isCacheablePackageResponse(500, 'text/plain')).toBe(false);
  });
});
````

````typescript
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import type { ProjectFile } from '../../src/types/latex';
import {
  detectBibliographyConfig,
  needsBibtex,
  needsMakeindex,
  resolveEntryFile,
  toEngineFiles,
} from '../../src/services/texProject';

function file(partial: Partial<ProjectFile> & { name: string }): ProjectFile {
  return {
    id: partial.id ?? partial.name,
    content: partial.content ?? '',
    type: partial.type ?? (partial.name.endsWith('.bib') ? 'bib' : 'tex'),
    ...partial,
  };
}

describe('resolveEntryFile', () => {
  it('prefers the explicitly marked entry', () => {
    const files = [
      file({ name: 'main.tex', content: '\\documentclass{article}' }),
      file({ name: 'paper.tex', content: '\\documentclass{article}', isEntry: true }),
    ];
    expect(resolveEntryFile(files)!.name).toBe('paper.tex');
  });

  it('falls back to main.tex by convention', () => {
    const files = [
      file({ name: 'sections/intro.tex', content: '\\section{Intro}' }),
      file({ name: 'main.tex', content: '\\documentclass{article}' }),
    ];
    expect(resolveEntryFile(files)!.name).toBe('main.tex');
  });

  it('finds the root by \\documentclass when nothing is marked', () => {
    // This is the case that matters: the open file is a fragment, and only the
    // root has a preamble, so only the root can compile.
    const files = [
      file({ name: 'sections/intro.tex', content: '\\section{Intro}\nText.' }),
      file({ name: 'thesis.tex', content: '\\documentclass[11pt]{report}\n' }),
    ];
    expect(resolveEntryFile(files)!.name).toBe('thesis.tex');
  });

  it('ignores a \\documentclass mentioned in a non-tex file', () => {
    const files = [
      file({ name: 'notes.md', content: '\\documentclass{article}', type: 'tex' }),
      file({ name: 'doc.tex', content: '\\documentclass{article}' }),
    ];
    expect(resolveEntryFile(files)!.name).toBe('doc.tex');
  });

  it('returns the only .tex file as a last resort', () => {
    const files = [file({ name: 'fragment.tex', content: 'Just text.' })];
    expect(resolveEntryFile(files)!.name).toBe('fragment.tex');
  });

  it('returns null when the project has no .tex file', () => {
    expect(resolveEntryFile([file({ name: 'refs.bib' })])).toBeNull();
    expect(resolveEntryFile([])).toBeNull();
  });
});

describe('toEngineFiles', () => {
  it('excludes the entry file, which is passed as the compile input', () => {
    const files = [
      file({ name: 'main.tex', content: '\\documentclass{article}' }),
      file({ name: 'sections/intro.tex', content: '\\section{Intro}' }),
    ];
    const paths = toEngineFiles(files, 'main.tex').map((f) => f.path);

    expect(paths).not.toContain('main.tex');
    expect(paths).toContain('sections/intro.tex');
  });

  it('passes image bytes as binary, not as a data URL string', () => {
    // A 1x1 PNG. Images carry bytes in dataUrl, with content empty — handing
    // TeX the empty content string means \includegraphics can never resolve.
    const png =
      'data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAEAAAABCAYAAAAfFcSJAAAADUlEQVR42mP8z8AAAwAB/AF+mEWRAAAAAElFTkSuQmCC';
    const files = [
      file({ name: 'main.tex', content: '\\documentclass{article}' }),
      file({ name: 'figures/logo.png', content: '', type: 'image', dataUrl: png }),
    ];

    const emitted = toEngineFiles(files, 'main.tex');
    const image = emitted.find((f) => f.path.endsWith('logo.png'))!;

    expect(image.content).toBeInstanceOf(Uint8Array);
    expect((image.content as Uint8Array).byteLength).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    // PNG magic number.
    expect((image.content as Uint8Array)[1]).toBe(0x50);
  });

  it('also exposes an image under its basename for partial references', () => {
    const png = 'data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgo=';
    const files = [
      file({ name: 'main.tex', content: '' }),
      file({ name: 'figures/logo.png', content: '', type: 'image', dataUrl: png }),
    ];

    const paths = toEngineFiles(files, 'main.tex').map((f) => f.path);
    // \includegraphics{logo} resolves by basename.
    expect(paths).toContain('logo.png');
    expect(paths).toContain('figures/logo.png');
  });

  it('emits each path at most once', () => {
    const files = [
      file({ name: 'main.tex', content: '' }),
      file({ name: 'refs.bib', content: '@book{a,title={T}}' }),
    ];
    const paths = toEngineFiles(files, 'main.tex').map((f) => f.path);
    expect(new Set(paths).size).toBe(paths.length);
  });
});

describe('needsBibtex', () => {
  it('is true only when a .bib exists and the document uses it', () => {
    const withBib = [file({ name: 'refs.bib', content: '' })];
    expect(needsBibtex(withBib, '\\bibliography{refs}')).toBe(true);
    expect(needsBibtex(withBib, '\\addbibresource{refs.bib}')).toBe(true);
  });

  it('is false with a .bib the document never references', () => {
    // Running BibTeX anyway emits "I found no \citation commands" into the log,
    // which would then surface as a diagnostic on a healthy document.
    const withBib = [file({ name: 'refs.bib', content: '' })];
    expect(needsBibtex(withBib, 'Plain text, no bibliography.')).toBe(false);
  });

  it('is false when the document cites but no .bib is present', () => {
    expect(needsBibtex([], '\\bibliography{refs}')).toBe(false);
  });
});

describe('detectBibliographyConfig', () => {
  it('detects standard bibliography with bib file present', () => {
    const withBib = [file({ name: 'refs.bib', content: '' })];
    const cfg = detectBibliographyConfig(withBib, '\\bibliography{refs}');
    expect(cfg.needed).toBe(true);
    expect(cfg.engine).toBe('bibtex');
    expect(cfg.hasBibFile).toBe(true);
    expect(cfg.usesBiblatex).toBe(false);
  });

  it('detects biblatex default (biber) and emits helpful warning without running bibtex8', () => {
    const withBib = [file({ name: 'refs.bib', content: '' })];
    const cfg = detectBibliographyConfig(withBib, '\\usepackage{biblatex}\n\\addbibresource{refs.bib}');
    expect(cfg.needed).toBe(false);
    expect(cfg.engine).toBe('biblatex-biber');
    expect(cfg.usesBiblatex).toBe(true);
    expect(cfg.warning).toContain('backend=bibtex');
  });

  it('allows biblatex when backend=bibtex is explicitly specified', () => {
    const withBib = [file({ name: 'refs.bib', content: '' })];
    const cfg = detectBibliographyConfig(withBib, '\\usepackage[backend=bibtex]{biblatex}\n\\addbibresource{refs.bib}');
    expect(cfg.needed).toBe(true);
    expect(cfg.engine).toBe('bibtex');
    expect(cfg.usesBiblatex).toBe(true);
  });

  it('returns needed: false when no bibliography directive or .bib is present', () => {
    const cfg = detectBibliographyConfig([], 'Simple article without citations.');
    expect(cfg.needed).toBe(false);
    expect(cfg.engine).toBe('none');
  });
});

describe('needsMakeindex', () => {
  it('detects index usage', () => {
    expect(needsMakeindex('\\makeindex\n\\printindex')).toBe(true);
    expect(needsMakeindex('No index here.')).toBe(false);
  });
});
````

````
# Teeex — environment configuration
# Copy to .env.local for local development, or set these in
# Cloudflare Pages Dashboard -> Settings -> Environment Variables.

# --- Supabase -----------------------------------------------------------------
VITE_SUPABASE_URL=https://your-project-id.supabase.co
VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.your-anon-public-key

# --- TeX Live package resolution ---------------------------------------------
# Only the `texlive-basic` package set is bundled with the engine. Any other
# package a document loads (IEEEtran, acmart, tikz, biblatex, ...) is fetched
# per-file from this endpoint at compile time. Without it, compilation is
# limited to the basic set and anything else fails with "File `x.sty' not
# found".
#
# Leave unset to use the public TeX Live 2026 server. Set to `off` to disable
# on-demand resolution entirely (offline / air-gapped use).
#
# Self-hosting is recommended for production (Option C): it removes the third-party runtime
# dependency and keeps document contents off someone else's server.
# See deploy/texlive-server/ for Dockerfile, Railway, Render, and Fly.io guides.
# VITE_TEXLIVE_REMOTE_ENDPOINT=https://your-texlive-service.up.railway.app

# --- Engine assets (build time, not runtime) ---------------------------------
# Origin that `npm run engine` downloads the WASM engine subset from. Point at
# your own mirror to avoid depending on upstream availability at build time.
# TEEEX_ENGINE_BASE_URL=https://texlyre.github.io/texlyre-busytex/core/busytex
````

````typescript
import React, { useState, useEffect } from 'react';
import { createPortal } from 'react-dom';
import {
  Zap,
  CheckCircle2,
  HardDrive,
  ShieldCheck,
  X,
  AlertCircle,
  DownloadCloud,
  RotateCcw,
} from 'lucide-react';
import { texEngine, type EngineStatus } from '../services/latexCompiler';
import { checkEngineCacheStatus, requestPersistentStorage, type EngineCacheStatus } from '../services/serviceWorker';
import { usePwaInstall } from '../hooks/usePwaInstall';

interface Props {
  status: EngineStatus;
  isOffline?: boolean;
  compact?: boolean;
}

export const EngineWarmupBadge: React.FC<Props> = ({ status, isOffline, compact = true }) => {
  const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = useState(false);
  const [cacheInfo, setCacheInfo] = useState<EngineCacheStatus | null>(null);
  const [isVerifying, setIsVerifying] = useState(false);
  const [hasRequestedPersist, setHasRequestedPersist] = useState(false);
  const [isPurging, setIsPurging] = useState(false);
  const { isInstallable, isInstalled, installApp } = usePwaInstall();

  useEffect(() => {
    checkEngineCacheStatus().then(setCacheInfo).catch(() => {});
  }, [status.phase]);

  // Dismiss modal on Escape key press
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!isOpen) return;
    const handleKeyDown = (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
      if (e.key === 'Escape') {
        setIsOpen(false);
      }
    };
    window.addEventListener('keydown', handleKeyDown);
    return () => window.removeEventListener('keydown', handleKeyDown);
  }, [isOpen]);

  const handleToggleOpen = () => {
    setIsOpen(prev => !prev);
    if (!isOpen) {
      checkEngineCacheStatus().then(setCacheInfo).catch(() => {});
    }
  };

  const handleRequestPersist = async () => {
    setIsVerifying(true);
    setHasRequestedPersist(true);
    await requestPersistentStorage();
    const next = await checkEngineCacheStatus();
    setCacheInfo(next);
    setIsVerifying(false);
  };

  const handlePurgeAndRetry = async () => {
    setIsPurging(true);
    try {
      if (typeof caches !== 'undefined') {
        const keys = await caches.keys();
        for (const key of keys) {
          if (key.startsWith('teeex-engine-')) {
            await caches.delete(key);
          }
        }
      }
      if (typeof indexedDB !== 'undefined') {
        await new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
          const req = indexedDB.deleteDatabase('EM_PRELOAD_CACHE');
          req.onsuccess = () => resolve();
          req.onerror = () => resolve();
          req.onblocked = () => resolve();
        });
      }
      const next = await checkEngineCacheStatus();
      setCacheInfo(next);
      texEngine.retryPrewarm(status.engine || 'pdflatex');
    } catch (err) {
      console.error('Failed to purge engine cache and retry:', err);
    } finally {
      setIsPurging(false);
    }
  };

  const isEngineReady = status.phase === 'ready' || Boolean(cacheInfo?.isEngineCached);
  const isPersisted = Boolean(cacheInfo?.persistedStorage);

  const renderModalPortal = () => {
    if (!isOpen) return null;
    const modalContent = renderTelemetryModal();
    if (typeof document !== 'undefined' && document.body) {
      return createPortal(modalContent, document.body);
    }
    return modalContent;
  };

  // 1. Failed Initialization State
  if (status.phase === 'failed') {
    return (
      <div className="engine-warmup-pill-container">
        <button
          type="button"
          onClick={handleToggleOpen}
          className="engine-warmup-pill failed"
          style={{ borderColor: 'rgba(244, 63, 94, 0.4)', color: '#fb7185' }}
          title={`TeX engine failed to initialize: ${status.error || 'Click to view telemetry'}`}
          aria-label="TeX Engine Failed"
        >
          <AlertCircle className="engine-warmup-icon text-rose-400" size={12} />
          <span className="engine-warmup-text">
            Engine Failed
          </span>
        </button>

        {renderModalPortal()}
      </div>
    );
  }

  // 2. Fetching / Downloading State
  if (status.phase === 'fetching') {
    return (
      <div className="engine-warmup-pill-container">
        <button
          type="button"
          onClick={handleToggleOpen}
          className="engine-warmup-pill fetching"
          title={`Click to view TeX engine download telemetry (${status.progress}%)`}
          aria-label={`Priming TeX Engine ${status.progress}%`}
        >
          <Zap className="engine-warmup-icon pulse-fast" size={12} />
          <span className="engine-warmup-text">
            Priming {status.progress}%
          </span>
          <div className="engine-warmup-mini-track">
            <div className="engine-warmup-mini-bar" style={{ width: `${status.progress}%` }} />
          </div>
        </button>

        {renderModalPortal()}
      </div>
    );
  }

  // 2. Ready & Cached / Idle State
  return (
    <div className="engine-warmup-pill-container">
      <button
        type="button"
        onClick={handleToggleOpen}
        className={`engine-warmup-pill ${isEngineReady ? 'ready' : 'idle'}`}
        title="Click to inspect local TeX engine cache & PWA storage"
        aria-label="TeX Engine Cache Status"
      >
        {isEngineReady ? (
          <CheckCircle2 className="engine-warmup-icon text-emerald-400" size={12} />
        ) : (
          <Zap className="engine-warmup-icon text-amber-400" size={12} />
        )}
        <span className="engine-warmup-text">
          {isOffline ? 'Offline' : isEngineReady ? (compact ? 'Ready' : 'TeX Live Primed (Offline Ready)') : 'Idle'}
        </span>
      </button>

      {renderModalPortal()}
    </div>
  );

  function renderTelemetryModal() {
    const totalMb = cacheInfo?.cachedBytes ? (cacheInfo.cachedBytes / 1024 / 1024).toFixed(1) : '138.2';

    return (
      <div className="engine-telemetry-backdrop" onClick={() => setIsOpen(false)}>
        <div className="engine-telemetry-card" onClick={e => e.stopPropagation()}>
          <div className="engine-telemetry-header">
            <div className="flex items-center gap-2" style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 8 }}>
              <HardDrive color="#38bdf8" size={16} />
              <h3 className="engine-telemetry-title">TeX Engine &amp; Storage Telemetry</h3>
            </div>
            <button
              type="button"
              onClick={() => setIsOpen(false)}
              className="engine-telemetry-close"
              aria-label="Close dialog"
            >
              <X size={15} />
            </button>
          </div>

          <div className="engine-telemetry-body">
            <div className="engine-metric-row">
              <span className="engine-metric-label">Engine Architecture</span>
              <span className="engine-metric-val">pdfLaTeX 2026 (WASM Emscripten)</span>
            </div>

            <div className="engine-metric-row">
              <span className="engine-metric-label">CacheStorage (sw.js)</span>
              <span className={`engine-metric-val ${cacheInfo?.hasWasm ? 'text-emerald-400' : 'text-amber-400'}`}>
                {cacheInfo?.hasWasm ? 'busytex.wasm (Cached)' : 'Pending Download'}
              </span>
            </div>

            <div className="engine-metric-row">
              <span className="engine-metric-label">IndexedDB (EM_PRELOAD_CACHE)</span>
              <span className={`engine-metric-val ${cacheInfo?.hasData ? 'text-emerald-400' : 'text-amber-400'}`}>
                {cacheInfo?.hasData ? 'texlive-basic.data (Cached)' : 'Pending Download'}
              </span>
            </div>

            <div className="engine-metric-row">
              <span className="engine-metric-label">Disk Storage Used</span>
              <span className="engine-metric-val font-mono">{totalMb} MB (on local disk)</span>
            </div>

            <div className="engine-metric-row">
              <span className="engine-metric-label">Eviction Protection</span>
              <span className="engine-metric-val flex items-center gap-1" style={{ display: 'inline-flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 4 }}>
                {isPersisted ? (
                  <>
                    <ShieldCheck size={14} color="#10b981" />
                    <span style={{ color: '#10b981', fontWeight: 600 }}>Persistent (Protected)</span>
                  </>
                ) : (
                  <>
                    <AlertCircle size={14} color="#f59e0b" />
                    <span style={{ color: '#f59e0b', fontWeight: 600 }}>Best-effort</span>
                  </>
                )}
              </span>
            </div>

            {!isPersisted && (
              <div style={{ display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column', gap: 6, marginTop: 4 }}>
                {isInstallable && !isInstalled && (
                  <button
                    type="button"
                    onClick={async () => {
                      await installApp();
                      const next = await checkEngineCacheStatus();
                      setCacheInfo(next);
                    }}
                    className="engine-persist-btn"
                    style={{
                      background: 'linear-gradient(135deg, #0284c7 0%, #0369a1 100%)',
                      borderColor: '#38bdf8',
                    }}
                  >
                    <DownloadCloud size={14} />
                    <span>Install Desktop App (PWA) for Eviction Immunity</span>
                  </button>
                )}

                <button
                  type="button"
                  onClick={handleRequestPersist}
                  disabled={isVerifying}
                  className="engine-persist-btn"
                >
                  <ShieldCheck size={14} />
                  <span>
                    {isVerifying
                      ? 'Contacting Browser Heuristics...'
                      : hasRequestedPersist
                        ? 'Requested • Granted via PWA / Regular Usage'
                        : 'Request Browser Eviction Immunity'}
                  </span>
                </button>

                <div style={{ fontSize: 10.5, color: 'var(--text-muted)', lineHeight: 1.4, padding: '2px 4px' }}>
                  Chromium (Chrome &amp; Edge) evaluates storage persistence automatically based on site engagement or PWA desktop installation.
                </div>
              </div>
            )}

            {status.error && (
              <div
                style={{
                  padding: '8px 12px',
                  background: 'rgba(244, 63, 94, 0.1)',
                  border: '1px solid rgba(244, 63, 94, 0.3)',
                  borderRadius: 8,
                  fontSize: 11.5,
                  lineHeight: 1.45,
                  color: '#fda4af',
                }}
              >
                <div style={{ fontWeight: 600, color: '#fb7185', marginBottom: 2 }}>
                  Initialization Diagnostic:
                </div>
                <div style={{ fontFamily: 'monospace', wordBreak: 'break-word' }}>
                  {status.error}
                </div>
              </div>
            )}

            <button
              type="button"
              onClick={handlePurgeAndRetry}
              disabled={isPurging}
              className="engine-purge-btn"
              title="Deletes locally cached engine binaries and restarts initialization"
            >
              <RotateCcw size={13} className={isPurging ? 'engine-spin' : ''} />
              <span>
                {isPurging ? 'Purging Local Caches & Restarting...' : 'Purge Engine Cache & Retry Priming'}
              </span>
            </button>

            <div className="engine-telemetry-tip">
              <p>
                <strong>Zero Cloud Queues:</strong> Teeex compiles LaTeX entirely on your device using WebAssembly. Once primed, documents typeset 100% offline with zero network latency.
              </p>
            </div>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
    );
  }
};
````
