````typescript
/**
 * Teeex Studio — Version History & Git-Grade Checkpoints Service
 * Manages per-project snapshot history, commit composer, working tree tracking,
 * local storage caching, and Supabase cloud push/pull synchronization.
 */

import type { ProjectFile } from '../types/latex';
import { getSupabaseClient, isSupabaseConnected } from './supabaseClient';
import { computeLineDiff } from './diffService';
import { saveCheckpointsOffline, loadCheckpointsOffline } from './offlineStorageService';

export interface CommitStats {
  additions: number;
  deletions: number;
  filesChanged: number;
}

export interface Checkpoint {
  id: string; // Commit SHA (e.g. 40-char or deterministic hash)
  shortSha: string; // 7-char short SHA (e.g. "a3f8c12")
  projectId: string;
  name: string; // Commit message title
  message?: string; // Explicit message alias
  description?: string; // Optional multiline commit notes
  timestamp: string; // Human-friendly time
  author: string;
  authorEmail?: string;
  files: ProjectFile[];
  stats?: CommitStats;
  parentId?: string | null;
  branch?: string; // default "main"
  isSyncedToCloud?: boolean;
  isAutoSave?: boolean;
  createdAt?: string;
}

export interface WorkingTreeFileStatus {
  fileId: string;
  fileName: string;
  status: 'modified' | 'added' | 'deleted';
  additions: number;
  deletions: number;
}

export interface WorkingTreeStatus {
  isClean: boolean;
  files: WorkingTreeFileStatus[];
  totalAdditions: number;
  totalDeletions: number;
}

export interface SyncStatus {
  ahead: number; // Local commits not yet pushed to cloud
  behind: number; // Remote commits not yet pulled locally
  isUpToDate: boolean;
}

const CHECKPOINTS_STORAGE_PREFIX = 'teeex_checkpoints_';
const BRANCHES_STORAGE_PREFIX = 'teeex_branches_';
const ACTIVE_BRANCH_STORAGE_PREFIX = 'teeex_active_branch_';
const MAX_CHECKPOINTS_PER_PROJECT = 50;

function getStorageKey(projectId: string): string {
  return `${CHECKPOINTS_STORAGE_PREFIX}${projectId}`;
}

function getBranchesStorageKey(projectId: string): string {
  return `${BRANCHES_STORAGE_PREFIX}${projectId}`;
}

function getActiveBranchStorageKey(projectId: string): string {
  return `${ACTIVE_BRANCH_STORAGE_PREFIX}${projectId}`;
}

/**
 * Retrieves the list of branch names for a project (defaults to ['main']).
 */
export function getProjectBranches(projectId: string): string[] {
  if (!projectId) return ['main'];
  try {
    const raw = localStorage.getItem(getBranchesStorageKey(projectId));
    if (raw) {
      const parsed = JSON.parse(raw);
      if (Array.isArray(parsed) && parsed.length > 0) {
        return Array.from(new Set(['main', ...parsed.filter(Boolean)]));
      }
    }
  } catch (err) {
    console.warn(`Failed to read branches for project ${projectId}:`, err);
  }
  return ['main'];
}

/**
 * Returns the active branch name for a project (defaults to 'main').
 */
export function getActiveBranch(projectId: string): string {
  if (!projectId) return 'main';
  try {
    const active = localStorage.getItem(getActiveBranchStorageKey(projectId));
    if (active && typeof active === 'string') {
      return active;
    }
  } catch {
    // fallback
  }
  return 'main';
}

/**
 * Sets the active branch for a project.
 */
export function setActiveBranch(projectId: string, branchName: string): void {
  if (!projectId || !branchName) return;
  try {
    const branches = getProjectBranches(projectId);
    if (!branches.includes(branchName)) {
      branches.push(branchName);
      localStorage.setItem(getBranchesStorageKey(projectId), JSON.stringify(branches));
    }
    localStorage.setItem(getActiveBranchStorageKey(projectId), branchName);
  } catch (err) {
    console.warn(`Failed to set active branch for project ${projectId}:`, err);
  }
}

/**
 * Creates a new branch for a project.
 */
export function createBranch(
  projectId: string,
  branchName: string,
  _sourceCommitId?: string
): { success: boolean; error?: string } {
  if (!projectId) return { success: false, error: 'Invalid project ID' };
  const cleanName = branchName.trim().replace(/\s+/g, '-').toLowerCase();
  if (!cleanName) return { success: false, error: 'Branch name cannot be empty' };
  if (!/^[a-z0-9_\-\/\.]+$/.test(cleanName)) {
    return { success: false, error: 'Branch name can only contain lowercase alphanumeric, -, _, /, and .' };
  }

  const branches = getProjectBranches(projectId);
  if (branches.includes(cleanName)) {
    return { success: false, error: `Branch "${cleanName}" already exists` };
  }

  branches.push(cleanName);
  try {
    localStorage.setItem(getBranchesStorageKey(projectId), JSON.stringify(branches));
    localStorage.setItem(getActiveBranchStorageKey(projectId), cleanName);
    return { success: true };
  } catch (err: unknown) {
    const e = err as { message?: string };
    return { success: false, error: e?.message || 'Failed to save branch' };
  }
}

/**
 * Deletes a branch from a project.
 */
export function deleteBranch(
  projectId: string,
  branchName: string
): { success: boolean; error?: string } {
  if (!projectId || !branchName) return { success: false, error: 'Invalid arguments' };
  if (branchName === 'main') return { success: false, error: 'Cannot delete default branch "main"' };
  if (branchName === getActiveBranch(projectId)) {
    return { success: false, error: 'Cannot delete currently active branch. Switch to another branch first.' };
  }

  const branches = getProjectBranches(projectId);
  const updated = branches.filter(b => b !== branchName);
  try {
    localStorage.setItem(getBranchesStorageKey(projectId), JSON.stringify(updated));
    return { success: true };
  } catch (err: unknown) {
    const e = err as { message?: string };
    return { success: false, error: e?.message || 'Failed to delete branch' };
  }
}

/**
 * Generates a deterministic or pseudorandom 7-character Git-style SHA.
 */
export function generateShortSha(seed?: string): string {
  if (seed) {
    let hash = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < seed.length; i++) {
      hash = (hash << 5) - hash + seed.charCodeAt(i);
      hash |= 0;
    }
    const hex = Math.abs(hash).toString(16).padStart(7, '0');
    return hex.slice(0, 7);
  }
  return Math.random().toString(16).slice(2, 9);
}

/**
 * Load all checkpoints/commits for a given project from localStorage.
 * If none exist, generates an initial baseline commit.
 */
export function loadProjectCheckpoints(
  projectId: string,
  currentFiles?: ProjectFile[],
  authorName = 'You'
): Checkpoint[] {
  if (!projectId) return [];

  const key = getStorageKey(projectId);
  try {
    const raw = localStorage.getItem(key);
    if (raw) {
      const parsed = JSON.parse(raw);
      if (Array.isArray(parsed) && parsed.length > 0) {
        return parsed.map((cp: any) => {
          const id = cp.id || `cp-${Date.now()}`;
          const shortSha = cp.shortSha || id.replace(/^cp-/, '').slice(0, 7) || generateShortSha(id);
          return {
            id,
            shortSha,
            projectId: cp.projectId || projectId,
            name: cp.name || cp.message || 'Commit',
            message: cp.message || cp.name || 'Commit',
            description: cp.description || '',
            timestamp: cp.timestamp || 'Just now',
            author: cp.author || 'Author',
            authorEmail: cp.authorEmail || '',
            files: Array.isArray(cp.files) ? cp.files : [],
            stats: cp.stats || { additions: 0, deletions: 0, filesChanged: 0 },
            parentId: cp.parentId ?? null,
            branch: cp.branch || 'main',
            isSyncedToCloud: cp.isSyncedToCloud ?? false,
            isAutoSave: Boolean(cp.isAutoSave),
            createdAt: cp.createdAt || new Date().toISOString(),
          };
        });
      }
    }
  } catch (err) {
    console.warn(`Failed to read checkpoints for project ${projectId}:`, err);
  }

  // Create initial baseline snapshot if files are available
  if (currentFiles && currentFiles.length > 0) {
    const now = new Date();
    const sha = generateShortSha(`init-${projectId}-${now.toISOString()}`);
    const initialCp: Checkpoint = {
      id: `commit-${sha}`,
      shortSha: sha,
      projectId,
      name: 'Initial Baseline',
      message: 'Initial Baseline',
      description: 'Initial project setup with root LaTeX documents and templates.',
      timestamp: now.toLocaleTimeString([], { hour: '2-digit', minute: '2-digit' }),
      author: authorName,
      files: JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(currentFiles)),
      stats: { additions: currentFiles.reduce((acc, f) => acc + (f.content?.split('\n').length || 0), 0), deletions: 0, filesChanged: currentFiles.length },
      parentId: null,
      branch: 'main',
      isSyncedToCloud: false,
      isAutoSave: false,
      createdAt: now.toISOString(),
    };
    saveProjectCheckpoints(projectId, [initialCp]);
    return [initialCp];
  }

  return [];
}

/**
 * Persist checkpoints for a given project with dual-layer architecture:
 * 1. Durable storage in IndexedDB (teeex_offline_db -> checkpoints_cache)
 * 2. Synchronous cache in localStorage with quota-exceeded fallback.
 */
export function saveProjectCheckpoints(projectId: string, checkpoints: Checkpoint[]): void {
  if (!projectId) return;
  const trimmed = (checkpoints || []).slice(0, MAX_CHECKPOINTS_PER_PROJECT);

  // 1. Durable write to IndexedDB
  saveCheckpointsOffline(projectId, trimmed).catch(() => {});

  // 2. Synchronous fast head cache in localStorage
  const key = getStorageKey(projectId);
  try {
    localStorage.setItem(key, JSON.stringify(trimmed));
  } catch (err) {
    console.warn(`[CheckpointsService] localStorage quota exceeded for project ${projectId}. Checkpoints are safely persisted in IndexedDB:`, err);
    try {
      // Retain the top 10 most recent commits in localStorage if full
      localStorage.setItem(key, JSON.stringify(trimmed.slice(0, 10)));
    } catch {
      // IndexedDB has the complete copy
    }
  }
}

/**
 * Hydrates checkpoints from IndexedDB if localStorage was cleared, missing,
 * or truncated due to quota limits.
 */
export async function hydrateCheckpointsFromOffline(projectId: string): Promise<Checkpoint[] | null> {
  if (!projectId) return null;
  try {
    const offlineCheckpoints = await loadCheckpointsOffline(projectId);
    if (offlineCheckpoints && offlineCheckpoints.length > 0) {
      const local = loadProjectCheckpoints(projectId);
      if (local.length < offlineCheckpoints.length) {
        saveProjectCheckpoints(projectId, offlineCheckpoints);
        return offlineCheckpoints;
      }
    }
  } catch {
    // Ignore hydration errors
  }
  return null;
}

/**
 * Computes the delta statistics (additions, deletions, filesChanged)
 * between a previous snapshot and a new set of files.
 */
export function computeCommitStats(
  oldFiles: ProjectFile[] = [],
  newFiles: ProjectFile[] = []
): CommitStats {
  let additions = 0;
  let deletions = 0;
  let filesChanged = 0;

  const oldMap = new Map<string, string>();
  for (const f of oldFiles) {
    oldMap.set(f.name, f.content || '');
  }

  const seenNames = new Set<string>();

  for (const nf of newFiles) {
    seenNames.add(nf.name);
    const oldContent = oldMap.get(nf.name);
    if (oldContent === undefined) {
      // Newly added file
      const lines = nf.content ? nf.content.split('\n').length : 0;
      additions += lines;
      filesChanged++;
    } else if (oldContent !== nf.content) {
      // Modified file
      const diff = computeLineDiff(oldContent, nf.content);
      additions += diff.additions;
      deletions += diff.deletions;
      filesChanged++;
    }
  }

  for (const [name, oldContent] of oldMap.entries()) {
    if (!seenNames.has(name)) {
      // Deleted file
      const lines = oldContent.split('\n').length;
      deletions += lines;
      filesChanged++;
    }
  }

  return { additions, deletions, filesChanged };
}

/**
 * Creates an intentional Git-grade commit with commit message, description,
 * author, calculated line change statistics, and short SHA.
 */
export function createCommit(
  projectId: string,
  message: string,
  author: string,
  files: ProjectFile[],
  description = '',
  branch?: string,
  authorEmail = ''
): Checkpoint {
  const current = loadProjectCheckpoints(projectId);
  const headCommit = current[0] || null;
  const resolvedBranch = branch || getActiveBranch(projectId) || 'main';

  const now = new Date();
  const sha = generateShortSha(`${projectId}-${message}-${now.getTime()}`);
  const stats = computeCommitStats(headCommit ? headCommit.files : [], files);

  const newCommit: Checkpoint = {
    id: `commit-${sha}`,
    shortSha: sha,
    projectId,
    name: message,
    message,
    description,
    timestamp: now.toLocaleTimeString([], { hour: '2-digit', minute: '2-digit' }),
    author: author || 'Author',
    authorEmail,
    files: JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(files)),
    stats,
    parentId: headCommit ? headCommit.id : null,
    branch: resolvedBranch,
    isSyncedToCloud: false,
    isAutoSave: false,
    createdAt: now.toISOString(),
  };

  const updated = [newCommit, ...current.filter(c => c.id !== newCommit.id)];

  // Prune excess if over limit
  if (updated.length > MAX_CHECKPOINTS_PER_PROJECT) {
    updated.length = MAX_CHECKPOINTS_PER_PROJECT;
  }

  saveProjectCheckpoints(projectId, updated);

  // Background push to Supabase Cloud if connected
  if (isSupabaseConnected()) {
    pushCheckpointToCloud(projectId, newCommit).then(res => {
      if (res.success) {
        newCommit.isSyncedToCloud = true;
        saveProjectCheckpoints(projectId, updated);
      }
    }).catch(err => {
      console.warn('Background commit cloud push error:', err);
    });
  }

  return newCommit;
}

/**
 * Backward-compatible wrapper for createCheckpoint.
 */
export function createCheckpoint(
  projectId: string,
  name: string,
  author: string,
  files: ProjectFile[],
  isAutoSave = false
): Checkpoint {
  if (!isAutoSave) {
    return createCommit(projectId, name, author, files);
  }

  const now = new Date();
  const sha = generateShortSha(`auto-${projectId}-${now.getTime()}`);
  const newCp: Checkpoint = {
    id: `cp-${now.getTime()}-${sha}`,
    shortSha: sha,
    projectId,
    name,
    message: name,
    timestamp: now.toLocaleTimeString([], { hour: '2-digit', minute: '2-digit' }),
    author: author || 'Author',
    files: JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(files)),
    isAutoSave: true,
    createdAt: now.toISOString(),
    isSyncedToCloud: false,
  };

  const current = loadProjectCheckpoints(projectId);
  const updated = [newCp, ...current];
  saveProjectCheckpoints(projectId, updated);
  return newCp;
}

/**
 * Computes the real-time working tree status (uncommitted changes compared to latest HEAD commit).
 */
export function getWorkingTreeStatus(
  currentFiles: ProjectFile[],
  headCommit: Checkpoint | null
): WorkingTreeStatus {
  if (!headCommit) {
    const totalAdditions = currentFiles.reduce((acc, f) => acc + (f.content?.split('\n').length || 0), 0);
    return {
      isClean: false,
      files: currentFiles.map(f => ({
        fileId: f.id,
        fileName: f.name,
        status: 'added',
        additions: f.content ? f.content.split('\n').length : 0,
        deletions: 0,
      })),
      totalAdditions,
      totalDeletions: 0,
    };
  }

  const headMap = new Map<string, string>();
  for (const f of headCommit.files) {
    headMap.set(f.name, f.content || '');
  }

  const filesStatus: WorkingTreeFileStatus[] = [];
  const seenNames = new Set<string>();
  let totalAdditions = 0;
  let totalDeletions = 0;

  for (const cf of currentFiles) {
    seenNames.add(cf.name);
    const headContent = headMap.get(cf.name);
    if (headContent === undefined) {
      const adds = cf.content ? cf.content.split('\n').length : 0;
      filesStatus.push({
        fileId: cf.id,
        fileName: cf.name,
        status: 'added',
        additions: adds,
        deletions: 0,
      });
      totalAdditions += adds;
    } else if (headContent !== cf.content) {
      const diff = computeLineDiff(headContent, cf.content);
      filesStatus.push({
        fileId: cf.id,
        fileName: cf.name,
        status: 'modified',
        additions: diff.additions,
        deletions: diff.deletions,
      });
      totalAdditions += diff.additions;
      totalDeletions += diff.deletions;
    }
  }

  for (const [name, headContent] of headMap.entries()) {
    if (!seenNames.has(name)) {
      const dels = headContent.split('\n').length;
      filesStatus.push({
        fileId: `del-${name}`,
        fileName: name,
        status: 'deleted',
        additions: 0,
        deletions: dels,
      });
      totalDeletions += dels;
    }
  }

  return {
    isClean: filesStatus.length === 0,
    files: filesStatus,
    totalAdditions,
    totalDeletions,
  };
}

/**
 * Remove a checkpoint from local storage and Supabase cloud.
 */
export async function deleteCheckpoint(projectId: string, checkpointId: string): Promise<Checkpoint[]> {
  const current = loadProjectCheckpoints(projectId);
  const updated = current.filter(cp => cp.id !== checkpointId);
  saveProjectCheckpoints(projectId, updated);

  const supabase = getSupabaseClient();
  if (supabase) {
    try {
      await supabase.from('checkpoints').delete().eq('id', checkpointId);
    } catch (err) {
      console.warn('Failed to delete checkpoint from cloud:', err);
    }
  }

  return updated;
}

/**
 * Push a single checkpoint to the Supabase checkpoints table.
 */
export async function pushCheckpointToCloud(
  projectId: string,
  checkpoint: Checkpoint
): Promise<{ success: boolean; error?: string }> {
  const supabase = getSupabaseClient();
  if (!supabase) return { success: false, error: 'Supabase client not connected' };

  try {
    const row = {
      id: checkpoint.id,
      project_id: projectId,
      name: checkpoint.name || checkpoint.message,
      timestamp: checkpoint.timestamp,
      author: checkpoint.author,
      files: checkpoint.files,
      created_at: checkpoint.createdAt || new Date().toISOString(),
    };

    const { error } = await supabase.from('checkpoints').upsert(row, { onConflict: 'id' });
    if (error) {
      console.warn('Checkpoint push to cloud error:', error.message);
      return { success: false, error: error.message };
    }
    return { success: true };
  } catch (err: unknown) {
    const e = err as { message?: string };
    return { success: false, error: e?.message || 'Cloud checkpoint sync failed' };
  }
}

/**
 * Push all un-synced local commits to Supabase Cloud.
 */
export async function pushCommitsToCloud(
  projectId: string
): Promise<{ success: boolean; pushedCount: number; error?: string }> {
  const local = loadProjectCheckpoints(projectId);
  const unsynced = local.filter(c => !c.isSyncedToCloud);

  if (unsynced.length === 0) {
    return { success: true, pushedCount: 0 };
  }

  let pushed = 0;
  for (const cp of unsynced) {
    const res = await pushCheckpointToCloud(projectId, cp);
    if (res.success) {
      cp.isSyncedToCloud = true;
      pushed++;
    }
  }

  saveProjectCheckpoints(projectId, local);
  return { success: true, pushedCount: pushed };
}

/**
 * Fetch remote checkpoints from Supabase and merge with local commits.
 */
export async function fetchProjectCheckpointsFromCloud(
  projectId: string
): Promise<{ success: boolean; checkpoints: Checkpoint[]; error?: string }> {
  const supabase = getSupabaseClient();
  if (!supabase || !projectId) {
    return { success: false, checkpoints: loadProjectCheckpoints(projectId), error: 'Not connected' };
  }

  try {
    const { data, error } = await supabase
      .from('checkpoints')
      .select('*')
      .eq('project_id', projectId)
      .order('created_at', { ascending: false });

    if (error) {
      return { success: false, checkpoints: loadProjectCheckpoints(projectId), error: error.message };
    }

    if (!data || data.length === 0) {
      return { success: true, checkpoints: loadProjectCheckpoints(projectId) };
    }

    const cloudCheckpoints: Checkpoint[] = data.map((r: any) => {
      const id = r.id;
      const shortSha = id.replace(/^(commit-|cp-)/, '').slice(0, 7) || generateShortSha(id);
      return {
        id,
        shortSha,
        projectId: r.project_id || projectId,
        name: r.name,
        message: r.name,
        description: r.description || '',
        timestamp: r.timestamp,
        author: r.author,
        files: Array.isArray(r.files) ? r.files : [],
        isSyncedToCloud: true,
        isAutoSave: r.name?.toLowerCase().startsWith('auto-save'),
        createdAt: r.created_at,
      };
    });

    // Merge cloud and local checkpoints without duplicates
    const local = loadProjectCheckpoints(projectId);
    const map = new Map<string, Checkpoint>();

    for (const cp of cloudCheckpoints) {
      map.set(cp.id, cp);
    }
    for (const cp of local) {
      if (!map.has(cp.id)) {
        map.set(cp.id, cp);
        // Push any local-only checkpoints to cloud in background
        pushCheckpointToCloud(projectId, cp).catch(() => {});
      }
    }

    const merged = Array.from(map.values()).sort((a, b) => {
      const timeA = new Date(a.createdAt || 0).getTime();
      const timeB = new Date(b.createdAt || 0).getTime();
      return timeB - timeA;
    });

    saveProjectCheckpoints(projectId, merged);
    return { success: true, checkpoints: merged };
  } catch (err: unknown) {
    const e = err as { message?: string };
    return { success: false, checkpoints: loadProjectCheckpoints(projectId), error: e?.message || 'Fetch failed' };
  }
}

/**
 * Calculates synchronization status (how many commits ahead or behind remote cloud).
 */
export function getSyncStatus(projectId: string): SyncStatus {
  const local = loadProjectCheckpoints(projectId);
  const ahead = local.filter(c => !c.isSyncedToCloud && !c.isAutoSave).length;
  return {
    ahead,
    behind: 0,
    isUpToDate: ahead === 0,
  };
}

/**
 * Helper to determine if files have changed significantly enough to warrant an autosave snapshot.
 */
export function haveFilesChanged(oldFiles: ProjectFile[], newFiles: ProjectFile[]): boolean {
  if (oldFiles.length !== newFiles.length) return true;
  for (const n of newFiles) {
    const matched = oldFiles.find(o => o.id === n.id || o.name === n.name);
    if (!matched) return true;
    if (matched.content !== n.content) return true;
  }
  return false;
}

/**
 * Creates an automatic version history milestone if files have changed significantly
 * since the most recent checkpoint.
 */
export function createAutoSaveCheckpointIfNeeded(
  projectId: string,
  files: ProjectFile[],
  author = 'Auto-Save'
): Checkpoint | null {
  if (!projectId || !files || files.length === 0) return null;
  const current = loadProjectCheckpoints(projectId);
  const latest = current[0];
  if (!latest || haveFilesChanged(latest.files, files)) {
    const stats = computeCommitStats(latest ? latest.files : [], files);
    if (stats.additions + stats.deletions > 0 || stats.filesChanged > 0) {
      const now = new Date();
      const timeStr = now.toLocaleTimeString([], { hour: '2-digit', minute: '2-digit' });
      return createCheckpoint(
        projectId,
        `Auto-save Milestone (${timeStr})`,
        author,
        files,
        true
      );
    }
  }
  return null;
}
````

````typescript
/**
 * Procedural Web Audio Engine for TeXCat Desk Companion.
 * Generates synthetic purr rumble, success chimes, warning chimes,
 * mechanical switch typing thocks, and playful sound effects.
 * Zero external audio files / MP3s required (< 2 KB footprint).
 * Strictly MUTED by default.
 */

export class DeskPetAudioEngine {
  private ctx: AudioContext | null = null;
  private isMuted: boolean = true;
  private volume: number = 0.6;
  private masterGain: GainNode | null = null;
  private activePurrStop: (() => void) | null = null;

  constructor(isMuted: boolean = true, volume: number = 0.6) {
    this.isMuted = isMuted;
    this.volume = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, volume));
  }

  public setMuted(muted: boolean): void {
    this.isMuted = muted;
    if (muted) {
      this.stopPurr();
      if (this.ctx && this.ctx.state === 'running') {
        void this.ctx.suspend();
      }
    } else {
      if (this.ctx && this.ctx.state === 'suspended') {
        void this.ctx.resume();
      }
    }
  }

  public getIsMuted(): boolean {
    return this.isMuted;
  }

  public setVolume(volume: number): void {
    this.volume = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, volume));
    if (this.masterGain && this.ctx) {
      this.masterGain.gain.setValueAtTime(this.volume, this.ctx.currentTime);
    }
  }

  public getVolume(): number {
    return this.volume;
  }

  private ensureContext(): AudioContext | null {
    if (this.isMuted || typeof window === 'undefined') return null;
    try {
      if (!this.ctx) {
        const AudioCtx = window.AudioContext || (window as unknown as { webkitAudioContext: typeof AudioContext }).webkitAudioContext;
        if (AudioCtx) {
          this.ctx = new AudioCtx();
          this.masterGain = this.ctx.createGain();
          this.masterGain.gain.setValueAtTime(this.volume, this.ctx.currentTime);
          this.masterGain.connect(this.ctx.destination);
        }
      }
      if (this.ctx && this.ctx.state === 'suspended') {
        void this.ctx.resume();
      }
      return this.ctx;
    } catch {
      return null;
    }
  }

  private getDestination(ctx: AudioContext): AudioNode {
    if (this.masterGain) {
      return this.masterGain;
    }
    return ctx.destination;
  }

  /**
   * Cat Purr: Generates a deep 28Hz modulated filtered white noise rumble with harmonic chest resonance.
   */
  public playPurr(durationMs = 1400): void {
    if (this.isMuted) return;
    const ctx = this.ensureContext();
    if (!ctx) return;

    this.stopPurr();

    try {
      const sampleRate = ctx.sampleRate;
      const bufferSize = Math.floor(sampleRate * (durationMs / 1000));
      const noiseBuffer = ctx.createBuffer(1, bufferSize, sampleRate);
      const data = noiseBuffer.getChannelData(0);

      // Generate soft pink/brownish noise
      let b0 = 0, b1 = 0;
      for (let i = 0; i < bufferSize; i++) {
        const white = Math.random() * 2 - 1;
        b0 = 0.99 * b0 + white * 0.05;
        b1 = 0.95 * b1 + white * 0.08;
        data[i] = (b0 + b1) * 0.5;
      }

      const noiseSource = ctx.createBufferSource();
      noiseSource.buffer = noiseBuffer;

      // Heavy low-pass filter (chest resonance around 75Hz)
      const filter = ctx.createBiquadFilter();
      filter.type = 'lowpass';
      filter.frequency.setValueAtTime(75, ctx.currentTime);

      // LFO modulation to pulse volume at 26Hz (cat vocal chord flutter)
      const lfo = ctx.createOscillator();
      lfo.frequency.setValueAtTime(26, ctx.currentTime);

      const lfoGain = ctx.createGain();
      lfoGain.gain.setValueAtTime(35, ctx.currentTime);
      lfo.connect(lfoGain);
      lfoGain.connect(filter.frequency);

      // Main volume envelope
      const gainNode = ctx.createGain();
      const now = ctx.currentTime;
      gainNode.gain.setValueAtTime(0, now);
      gainNode.gain.linearRampToValueAtTime(0.35, now + 0.15);
      gainNode.gain.linearRampToValueAtTime(0.35, now + (durationMs / 1000) - 0.2);
      gainNode.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.001, now + (durationMs / 1000));

      noiseSource.connect(filter);
      filter.connect(gainNode);
      gainNode.connect(this.getDestination(ctx));

      noiseSource.start(now);
      lfo.start(now);

      const stopTime = now + (durationMs / 1000);
      noiseSource.stop(stopTime);
      lfo.stop(stopTime);

      this.activePurrStop = () => {
        try {
          noiseSource.stop();
          lfo.stop();
        } catch {
          // Ignore
        }
      };
    } catch {
      // Ignore audio synthesis errors
    }
  }

  public stopPurr(): void {
    if (this.activePurrStop) {
      this.activePurrStop();
      this.activePurrStop = null;
    }
  }

  /**
   * Success Chime: Ascending major triad chord (C5 523Hz -> E5 659Hz -> G5 784Hz).

    if (!ctx) return;

    try {
      const now = ctx.currentTime;
      const notes = [523.25, 659.25, 783.99]; // C5, E5, G5

      notes.forEach((freq, idx) => {
        const osc = ctx.createOscillator();
        const gain = ctx.createGain();

        osc.type = 'sine';
        osc.frequency.setValueAtTime(freq, now + idx * 0.08);

        const startTime = now + idx * 0.08;
        const endTime = startTime + 0.9;

        gain.gain.setValueAtTime(0, startTime);
        gain.gain.linearRampToValueAtTime(0.2, startTime + 0.02);
        gain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.001, endTime);

        osc.connect(gain);
        gain.connect(this.getDestination(ctx));

        osc.start(startTime);

      });

      // Ignore

  }
````

````typescript
/**
 * Diff Service for Teeex
 * Computes high-performance line-by-line and intra-line word differences
 * between file revisions using Longest Common Subsequence (LCS).
 */

import type { ProjectFile } from '../types/latex';

export type DiffType = 'added' | 'removed' | 'unchanged';

export interface DiffToken {
  text: string;
  type: 'added' | 'removed' | 'unchanged';
}

export interface DiffLine {
  type: DiffType;
  oldLineNumber?: number;
  newLineNumber?: number;
  text: string;
  tokens?: DiffToken[];
}

export interface SplitDiffRow {
  left?: {
    lineNumber: number;
    text: string;
    type: 'removed' | 'unchanged';
    tokens?: DiffToken[];
  };
  right?: {
    lineNumber: number;
    text: string;
    type: 'added' | 'unchanged';
    tokens?: DiffToken[];
  };
}

export interface DiffResult {
  lines: DiffLine[];
  splitRows: SplitDiffRow[];
  additions: number;
  deletions: number;
  unchanged: number;
}

export interface FileDiffSummary {
  fileId: string;
  fileName: string;
  status: 'modified' | 'added' | 'deleted' | 'unchanged';
  additions: number;
  deletions: number;
  oldContent: string;
  newContent: string;
  diff: DiffResult;
}

/**
 * Tokenizes a string into words, LaTeX control sequences, punctuation, and whitespace.
 */
function tokenizeWords(str: string): string[] {
  if (!str) return [];
  // Matches LaTeX commands (\section, \alpha), words, spaces, or individual punctuation
  const regex = /(\\[a-zA-Z@]+|\s+|[a-zA-Z0-9_]+|[^\s\w\\])/g;
  const tokens: string[] = [];
  let m: RegExpExecArray | null;
  while ((m = regex.exec(str)) !== null) {
    tokens.push(m[0]);
  }
  return tokens.length > 0 ? tokens : [str];
}

/**
 * Computes word-level diff between two lines using LCS.
 */
export function computeWordDiff(
  oldLine: string,
  newLine: string
): { oldTokens: DiffToken[]; newTokens: DiffToken[] } {
  const tokA = tokenizeWords(oldLine);
  const tokB = tokenizeWords(newLine);

  const lenA = tokA.length;
  const lenB = tokB.length;

  // Bounded check for extremely long single lines (fallback to single token)
  if (lenA > 250 || lenB > 250) {
    return {
      oldTokens: [{ text: oldLine, type: 'removed' }],
      newTokens: [{ text: newLine, type: 'added' }],
    };
  }

  // LCS Dynamic Programming table
  const dp: number[][] = Array.from({ length: lenA + 1 }, () => new Array(lenB + 1).fill(0));
  for (let i = 1; i <= lenA; i++) {
    for (let j = 1; j <= lenB; j++) {
      if (tokA[i - 1] === tokB[j - 1]) {
        dp[i][j] = dp[i - 1][j - 1] + 1;
      } else {
        dp[i][j] = Math.max(dp[i - 1][j], dp[i][j - 1]);
      }
    }
  }

  const oldTokensRev: DiffToken[] = [];
  const newTokensRev: DiffToken[] = [];

  let i = lenA;
  let j = lenB;

  while (i > 0 || j > 0) {
    if (i > 0 && j > 0 && tokA[i - 1] === tokB[j - 1]) {
      oldTokensRev.push({ text: tokA[i - 1], type: 'unchanged' });
      newTokensRev.push({ text: tokB[j - 1], type: 'unchanged' });
      i--;
      j--;
    } else if (j > 0 && (i === 0 || dp[i][j - 1] >= dp[i - 1][j])) {
      newTokensRev.push({ text: tokB[j - 1], type: 'added' });
      j--;
    } else if (i > 0 && (j === 0 || dp[i][j - 1] < dp[i - 1][j])) {
      oldTokensRev.push({ text: tokA[i - 1], type: 'removed' });
      i--;
    }
  }

  return {
    oldTokens: oldTokensRev.reverse(),
    newTokens: newTokensRev.reverse(),
  };
}

/**
 * Computes line-by-line diff using prefix/suffix Heckel-Myers trimming + LCS,
 * enhancing replaced lines with intra-line word highlights in sub-millisecond time.
 */
export function computeLineDiff(oldContent: string, newContent: string): DiffResult {
  if (oldContent === newContent) {
    const linesA = oldContent === '' ? [] : oldContent.split('\n');
    const lines: DiffLine[] = linesA.map((text, i) => ({
      type: 'unchanged',
      oldLineNumber: i + 1,
      newLineNumber: i + 1,
      text,
      tokens: [{ text, type: 'unchanged' }],
    }));
    const splitRows: SplitDiffRow[] = linesA.map((text, i) => ({
      left: { lineNumber: i + 1, text, type: 'unchanged', tokens: [{ text, type: 'unchanged' }] },
      right: { lineNumber: i + 1, text, type: 'unchanged', tokens: [{ text, type: 'unchanged' }] },
    }));
    return {
      lines,
      splitRows,
      additions: 0,
      deletions: 0,
      unchanged: linesA.length,
    };
  }

  const linesA = oldContent === '' ? [] : oldContent.split('\n');
  const linesB = newContent === '' ? [] : newContent.split('\n');

  const m = linesA.length;
  const n = linesB.length;

  // Handle completely empty old content (pure addition)
  if (m === 0) {
    const lines: DiffLine[] = linesB.map((text, i) => ({
      type: 'added',
      newLineNumber: i + 1,
      text,
      tokens: [{ text, type: 'added' }],
    }));
    const splitRows: SplitDiffRow[] = linesB.map((text, i) => ({
      right: { lineNumber: i + 1, text, type: 'added', tokens: [{ text, type: 'added' }] },
    }));
    return {
      lines,
      splitRows,
      additions: n,
      deletions: 0,
      unchanged: 0,
    };
  }

  // Handle completely empty new content (pure deletion)
  if (n === 0) {
    const lines: DiffLine[] = linesA.map((text, i) => ({
      type: 'removed',
      oldLineNumber: i + 1,
      text,
      tokens: [{ text, type: 'removed' }],
    }));
    const splitRows: SplitDiffRow[] = linesA.map((text, i) => ({
      left: { lineNumber: i + 1, text, type: 'removed', tokens: [{ text, type: 'removed' }] },
    }));
    return {
      lines,
      splitRows,
      additions: 0,
      deletions: m,
      unchanged: 0,
    };
  }

  // 1. Prefix trimming: match identical lines at start
  let prefix = 0;
  while (prefix < m && prefix < n && linesA[prefix] === linesB[prefix]) {
    prefix++;
  }

  // 2. Suffix trimming: match identical lines at end
  let suffix = 0;
  while (
    suffix < (m - prefix) &&
    suffix < (n - prefix) &&
    linesA[m - 1 - suffix] === linesB[n - 1 - suffix]
  ) {
    suffix++;
  }

  const prefixLines: DiffLine[] = [];
  const prefixSplitRows: SplitDiffRow[] = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < prefix; i++) {
    const text = linesA[i];
    prefixLines.push({
      type: 'unchanged',
      oldLineNumber: i + 1,
      newLineNumber: i + 1,
      text,
      tokens: [{ text, type: 'unchanged' }],
    });
    prefixSplitRows.push({
      left: { lineNumber: i + 1, text, type: 'unchanged', tokens: [{ text, type: 'unchanged' }] },
      right: { lineNumber: i + 1, text, type: 'unchanged', tokens: [{ text, type: 'unchanged' }] },
    });
  }

  const suffixLines: DiffLine[] = [];
  const suffixSplitRows: SplitDiffRow[] = [];
  for (let s = suffix - 1; s >= 0; s--) {
    const oldIdx = m - 1 - s;
    const newIdx = n - 1 - s;
    const text = linesA[oldIdx];
    suffixLines.push({
      type: 'unchanged',
      oldLineNumber: oldIdx + 1,
      newLineNumber: newIdx + 1,
      text,
      tokens: [{ text, type: 'unchanged' }],
    });
    suffixSplitRows.push({
      left: { lineNumber: oldIdx + 1, text, type: 'unchanged', tokens: [{ text, type: 'unchanged' }] },
      right: { lineNumber: newIdx + 1, text, type: 'unchanged', tokens: [{ text, type: 'unchanged' }] },
    });
  }

  // 3. Middle range diffing
  const midA = linesA.slice(prefix, m - suffix);
  const midB = linesB.slice(prefix, n - suffix);
  const midM = midA.length;
  const midN = midB.length;

  let middleLines: DiffLine[] = [];
  const middleSplitRows: SplitDiffRow[] = [];

  if (midM === 0 && midN === 0) {
    // Both prefix and suffix covered entire files
  } else if (midM === 0) {
    // Pure additions in middle
    for (let j = 0; j < midN; j++) {
      const text = midB[j];
      const newLineNumber = prefix + j + 1;
      middleLines.push({
        type: 'added',
        newLineNumber,
        text,
        tokens: [{ text, type: 'added' }],
      });
      middleSplitRows.push({
        right: { lineNumber: newLineNumber, text, type: 'added', tokens: [{ text, type: 'added' }] },
      });
    }
  } else if (midN === 0) {
    // Pure deletions in middle
    for (let i = 0; i < midM; i++) {
      const text = midA[i];
      const oldLineNumber = prefix + i + 1;
      middleLines.push({
        type: 'removed',
        oldLineNumber,
        text,
        tokens: [{ text, type: 'removed' }],
      });
      middleSplitRows.push({
        left: { lineNumber: oldLineNumber, text, type: 'removed', tokens: [{ text, type: 'removed' }] },
      });
    }
  } else {
    // Bounded LCS on middle range using flat 1D Int32Array
    const maxMid = 2000;
    const effA = midA.slice(0, maxMid);
    const effB = midB.slice(0, maxMid);
    const effM = effA.length;
    const effN = effB.length;

    const stride = effN + 1;
    const dp = new Int32Array((effM + 1) * stride);

    for (let i = 1; i <= effM; i++) {
      const rowOffset = i * stride;
      const prevRowOffset = (i - 1) * stride;
      const valA = effA[i - 1];
      for (let j = 1; j <= effN; j++) {
        if (valA === effB[j - 1]) {
          dp[rowOffset + j] = dp[prevRowOffset + (j - 1)] + 1;
        } else {
          const up = dp[prevRowOffset + j];
          const left = dp[rowOffset + (j - 1)];
          dp[rowOffset + j] = up > left ? up : left;
        }
      }
    }

    const revMidLines: DiffLine[] = [];
    let bi = effM;
    let bj = effN;

    while (bi > 0 || bj > 0) {
      const rowOffset = bi * stride;
      const prevRowOffset = (bi - 1) * stride;
      if (bi > 0 && bj > 0 && effA[bi - 1] === effB[bj - 1]) {
        revMidLines.push({
          type: 'unchanged',
          oldLineNumber: prefix + bi,
          newLineNumber: prefix + bj,
          text: effA[bi - 1],
          tokens: [{ text: effA[bi - 1], type: 'unchanged' }],
        });
        bi--;
        bj--;
      } else if (bj > 0 && (bi === 0 || dp[rowOffset + (bj - 1)] >= dp[prevRowOffset + bj])) {
        revMidLines.push({
          type: 'added',
          newLineNumber: prefix + bj,
          text: effB[bj - 1],
        });
        bj--;
      } else if (bi > 0 && (bj === 0 || dp[rowOffset + (bj - 1)] < dp[prevRowOffset + bj])) {
        revMidLines.push({
          type: 'removed',
          oldLineNumber: prefix + bi,
          text: effA[bi - 1],
        });
        bi--;
      }
    }

    middleLines = revMidLines.reverse();

    // Build paired split rows for middle with intra-line word diffs
    let k = 0;
    while (k < middleLines.length) {
      const cur = middleLines[k];
      if (cur.type === 'unchanged') {
        middleSplitRows.push({
          left: { lineNumber: cur.oldLineNumber!, text: cur.text, type: 'unchanged', tokens: cur.tokens },
          right: { lineNumber: cur.newLineNumber!, text: cur.text, type: 'unchanged', tokens: cur.tokens },
        });
        k++;
      } else if (cur.type === 'removed') {
        if (k + 1 < middleLines.length && middleLines[k + 1].type === 'added') {
          const next = middleLines[k + 1];
          const { oldTokens, newTokens } = computeWordDiff(cur.text, next.text);
          cur.tokens = oldTokens;
          next.tokens = newTokens;
          middleSplitRows.push({
            left: { lineNumber: cur.oldLineNumber!, text: cur.text, type: 'removed', tokens: oldTokens },
            right: { lineNumber: next.newLineNumber!, text: next.text, type: 'added', tokens: newTokens },
          });
          k += 2;
        } else {
          cur.tokens = [{ text: cur.text, type: 'removed' }];
          middleSplitRows.push({
            left: { lineNumber: cur.oldLineNumber!, text: cur.text, type: 'removed', tokens: cur.tokens },
          });
          k++;
        }
      } else if (cur.type === 'added') {
        cur.tokens = [{ text: cur.text, type: 'added' }];
        middleSplitRows.push({
          right: { lineNumber: cur.newLineNumber!, text: cur.text, type: 'added', tokens: cur.tokens },
        });
        k++;
      } else {
        k++;
      }
    }
  }

  // Combine prefix + middle + suffix
  const allLines = [...prefixLines, ...middleLines, ...suffixLines];
  const allSplitRows = [...prefixSplitRows, ...middleSplitRows, ...suffixSplitRows];

  let additions = 0;
  let deletions = 0;
  let unchanged = 0;

  for (const l of allLines) {
    if (l.type === 'added') additions++;
    else if (l.type === 'removed') deletions++;
    else unchanged++;
  }

  return {
    lines: allLines,
    splitRows: allSplitRows,
    additions,
    deletions,
    unchanged,
  };
}

/**
 * Computes multi-file diff summary across two project file snapshots.
 */
export function computeProjectFileDiffs(
  oldFiles: ProjectFile[],
  newFiles: ProjectFile[]
): FileDiffSummary[] {
  const fileMap = new Map<string, { oldFile?: ProjectFile; newFile?: ProjectFile }>();

  // Map old files
  for (const f of oldFiles) {
    fileMap.set(f.id, { oldFile: f });
  }

  // Match or add new files
  for (const f of newFiles) {
    const existing = fileMap.get(f.id) || Array.from(fileMap.values()).find(v => v.oldFile?.name === f.name);
    if (existing) {
      existing.newFile = f;
    } else {
      fileMap.set(f.id, { newFile: f });
    }
  }

  const summaries: FileDiffSummary[] = [];

  for (const [fileId, { oldFile, newFile }] of fileMap.entries()) {
    const fileName = newFile?.name || oldFile?.name || 'file';
    const oldContent = oldFile?.content || '';
    const newContent = newFile?.content || '';

    let status: 'modified' | 'added' | 'deleted' | 'unchanged' = 'unchanged';
    if (!oldFile && newFile) {
      status = 'added';
    } else if (oldFile && !newFile) {
      status = 'deleted';
    } else if (oldContent !== newContent) {
      status = 'modified';
    }

    const diff = computeLineDiff(oldContent, newContent);

    summaries.push({
      fileId,
      fileName,
      status,
      additions: diff.additions,
      deletions: diff.deletions,
      oldContent,
      newContent,
      diff,
    });
  }

  // Sort: Modified first, then Added, then Deleted, then Unchanged
  const order = { modified: 0, added: 1, deleted: 2, unchanged: 3 };
  summaries.sort((a, b) => order[a.status] - order[b.status] || a.fileName.localeCompare(b.fileName));

  return summaries;
}
````

````typescript
/**
 * Fast search and filtering for LaTeX snippets
 */
export function searchLatexSnippets(query: string): LatexSnippet[] {
  const clean = query.trim().toLowerCase().replace(/^\\/, '');
  if (!clean) return LATEX_SNIPPETS.slice(0, 10);

  return LATEX_SNIPPETS.filter(s => {
    return (
      s.trigger.toLowerCase().startsWith(clean) ||
      s.label.toLowerCase().includes(clean) ||
      s.description.toLowerCase().includes(clean)
    );
  }).slice(0, 8);
}
````

## File: src/services/pdfExporter.ts
````typescript
/**
 * Teeex — PDF export.
 *
 * Export writes out the exact bytes the TeX engine produced and the preview is
 * displaying. There is no second rendering path, so there is nothing for
 * export to get wrong.
 *
 * This replaces a DOM-print exporter that cloned the preview markup into an
 * iframe and called window.print() after a fixed 600 ms. That approach could
 * not work: the output depended on the user's print dialog (paper size,
 * margins, headers, scale), the delay raced webfont loading so line breaking
 * differed from the preview, and it re-derived layout from CSS instead of from
 * the document.
 */

/** Turns a project or document title into a safe, readable file name. */
export function pdfFileName(title: string): string {
  const base = title
    .normalize('NFKD')
    // Strip characters that are invalid in file names on any common platform.
    .replace(/[\\/:*?"<>|\u0000-\u001f]/g, '')
    .replace(/\s+/g, '_')
    .replace(/_{2,}/g, '_')
    .replace(/^[_.]+|[_.]+$/g, '')
    .slice(0, 120);

  return `${base || 'document'}.pdf`;
}

/**
 * Saves compiled PDF bytes to disk.
 *
 * Copies into a fresh buffer before wrapping in a Blob: the same bytes may be
 * held by the viewer, and transferring or detaching a shared ArrayBuffer here
 * would corrupt what is on screen.
 */
export function downloadPdf(bytes: Uint8Array, title: string): void {
  if (!bytes || bytes.byteLength === 0) {
    throw new Error('There is no compiled PDF to export yet.');
  }

  const owned = new Uint8Array(bytes.byteLength);
  owned.set(bytes);

  const blob = new Blob([owned as unknown as BlobPart], { type: 'application/pdf' });
  const url = URL.createObjectURL(blob);

  try {
    const anchor = document.createElement('a');
    anchor.href = url;
    anchor.download = pdfFileName(title);
    anchor.rel = 'noopener';
    anchor.style.display = 'none';
    document.body.append(anchor);
    anchor.click();
    anchor.remove();
  } finally {
    // Revoked on the next task so the navigation has started by then; doing it
    // synchronously cancels the download in some browsers.
    setTimeout(() => URL.revokeObjectURL(url), 0);
  }
}

/** Opens the compiled PDF in a new tab, for printing or an external viewer. */
export function openPdfInNewTab(bytes: Uint8Array): void {
  if (!bytes || bytes.byteLength === 0) {
    throw new Error('There is no compiled PDF to open yet.');
  }

  const owned = new Uint8Array(bytes.byteLength);
  owned.set(bytes);

  const url = URL.createObjectURL(
    new Blob([owned as unknown as BlobPart], { type: 'application/pdf' }),
  );
  const opened = window.open(url, '_blank', 'noopener');

  if (!opened) {
    URL.revokeObjectURL(url);
    throw new Error('The browser blocked opening the PDF. Allow pop-ups for this site, or use Download instead.');
  }

  // The new tab owns the URL now; release our handle once it has loaded.
  setTimeout(() => URL.revokeObjectURL(url), 60_000);
}
````

````typescript
\\author{Dr. Elena Rostova \\and Dr. Marcus Chen \\and Dr. Aris Thorne}
\\date{\\today}

\\begin{document}

\\maketitle

\\begin{abstract}
Quantum state tomography is essential for characterizing quantum information processors. However, conventional maximum likelihood estimation scales exponentially with the number of qubits $N$. In this paper, we propose an attention-augmented transformer framework capable of reconstructing density matrices $\\rho$ with $99.4\\%$ fidelity in polynomial time.
\\end{abstract}

\\section{Introduction}
Characterization of quantum computational devices requires robust reconstruction of quantum density operators. Given an ensemble of Pauli measurements, reconstructing the density operator $\\rho \\in \\mathbb{C}^{2^N \\times 2^N}$ poses a fundamental challenge in quantum verification \\cite{thorne2025quantum}.

Traditional tomography relies on matrix inversion and compressed sensing. Our approach utilizes neural representations where the probability distribution $P(\\sigma)$ of measurement outcomes is modeled directly:
\\begin{equation}
P(\\boldsymbol{\\sigma}) = \\frac{1}{Z} \\exp\\left( -\\sum_{j=1}^M \\theta_j \\phi_j(\\boldsymbol{\\sigma}) \\right)
\\end{equation}

\\section{System Architecture}
The quantum variational autoencoder comprises an encoder module $E_\\phi$ that maps projective basis states to continuous latent representations:
\\begin{equation}
\\mathcal{L}_{\\text{rec}}(\\theta, \\phi) = \\mathbb{E}_{x \\sim \\mathcal{D}}\\left[ -\\log p_\\theta(x | z) \\right] + D_{\\text{KL}}\\left( q_\\phi(z|x) \\parallel p(z) \\right)
\\end{equation}

\\section{Experimental Results}
We evaluated our framework against synthetic GHZ and W-states across system sizes up to $N = 12$ qubits. Table I summarizes the reconstruction fidelity and convergence latency.

\\begin{table}[htbp]
\\centering
\\caption{Reconstruction Fidelity and Execution Latency Across Quantum State Families}
\\label{tab:fidelity}
\\begin{tabular}{l c c c}
\\hline

\\hline
GHZ State & 4 & 99.82 & 14.2 \\\\
W-State & 6 & 99.45 & 28.6 \\\\
Cluster State & 8 & 98.91 & 62.4 \\\\
Random Haar & 10 & 97.80 & 145.0 \\\\
\\hline
\\end{tabular}
\\end{table}

\\section{Conclusion}
We demonstrated that attention-based quantum state tomography scales effectively beyond the reach of standard convex optimization solvers. Future work will explore real-time hardware deployment on superconducting architectures.

\\bibliographystyle{plain}
\\bibliography{references}

\\end{document}`;
````

## File: src/services/texLog.ts
````typescript
/**
 * Teeex — pdfTeX / LaTeX log parser.
 *
 * TeX's console log is the only channel through which the engine reports what
 * it did. Parsing it properly is what separates "compilation failed" from
 * "line 42 of sections/intro.tex uses \includegraphics but graphicx is not
 * loaded".
 *
 * Three details that naive parsers get wrong, and that this module handles:
 *
 *  1. Line wrapping. TeX hard-wraps log output at `max_print_line` (79 by
 *     default), splitting messages mid-word. Lines must be rejoined before
 *     matching or every pattern anchored past column 79 silently fails.
 *
 *  2. File attribution. TeX reports `(./file.tex` on open and `)` on close.
 *     Without tracking that stack, every diagnostic gets blamed on the root
 *     file, so errors inside \input-ed files point at the wrong document.
 *
 *  3. Classification. "File `foo.sty' not found" is recoverable by loading a
 *     package; "Emergency stop" is not. Collapsing both to "error" throws away
 *     the only information that lets the UI offer a fix.
 *
 * Kept free of engine and DOM dependencies so it is directly unit-testable.
 */

export type DiagnosticSeverity = 'error' | 'warning' | 'info';

export type DiagnosticCode =
  | 'missing-package'
  | 'missing-file'
  | 'missing-graphic'
  | 'undefined-control-sequence'
  | 'undefined-environment'
  | 'missing-citation'
  | 'missing-reference'
  | 'duplicate-label'
  | 'missing-glyph'
  | 'font-substitution'
  | 'rerun-required'
  | 'overfull-box'
  | 'underfull-box'
  | 'syntax'
  | 'fatal'
  | 'other';

export interface DiagnosticSuggestedFix {
  title: string;
  description: string;
  replacement: string;
  startLine: number;
  endLine: number;
}

export interface CompileDiagnostic {
  id: string;
  severity: DiagnosticSeverity;
  code: DiagnosticCode;
  message: string;
  /** Source file TeX was reading, relative to the project root, when available. */
  file?: string;
  line?: number;
  /** Set for diagnostics that span a range, e.g. bad boxes ("at lines 23--25"). */
  endLine?: number;
  /** The `l.NN ...` source excerpt TeX echoed, when present. */
  context?: string;
  /** Actionable next step, only when one can be stated with confidence. */
  hint?: string;
  /** Actionable 1-click code replacement when applicable. */
  suggestedFix?: DiagnosticSuggestedFix;
  /** Verbatim log lines this diagnostic was derived from. */
  raw: string;
}

export interface TexLogParseResult {
  diagnostics: CompileDiagnostic[];
  /** Package names from "File `x.sty' not found" — resolvable on demand. */
  missingPackages: string[];
  /** Non-.sty inputs TeX could not find (graphics, .bib, \input targets). */
  missingFiles: string[];
  /** True when LaTeX asked for another pass to settle refs/labels/TOC. */
  rerunRequired: boolean;
  /** True when TeX aborted without producing output. */
  fatal: boolean;
  /** Files TeX actually opened, in first-seen order. */
  filesRead: string[];
}

const DEFAULT_MAX_PRINT_LINE = 79;

/**
 * Markers that always begin a logical log line. A wrapped continuation never
 * starts with one of these, so they act as a guard against gluing together two
 * genuinely distinct lines that happen to sit at the wrap column.
 */
const LINE_START_MARKERS = [
  '!',
  'l.',
  'Overfull',
  'Underfull',
  'LaTeX Warning:',
  'LaTeX Font Warning:',
  'LaTeX Info:',
  'Package ',
  'Class ',
  'Document Class:',
  'Missing character:',
  'No file',
  'Output written',
  'Transcript written',
  'This is pdfTeX',
  'This is XeTeX',
  'This is LuaHBTeX',
  '***',
  '==>',
];

function startsLogicalLine(line: string): boolean {
  if (line.length === 0) return true;
  return LINE_START_MARKERS.some((marker) => line.startsWith(marker));
}

/**
 * Rejoins lines TeX wrapped at `maxPrintLine`.
 *
 * A line is treated as wrapped when it is exactly at the wrap width and the
 * following line does not itself begin a new logical record. This is a
 * heuristic — a real line of exactly 79 characters followed by a continuation
 * is indistinguishable from a wrap — but it is the same heuristic every
 * production LaTeX log parser uses, and erring toward joining recovers far more
 * messages than it corrupts.
 */
export function unwrapLogLines(
  log: string,
  maxPrintLine: number = DEFAULT_MAX_PRINT_LINE,
): string[] {
  const rawLines = log.replace(/\r\n?/g, '\n').split('\n');
  const out: string[] = [];

  for (const raw of rawLines) {
    const previous = out[out.length - 1];
    const previousWasWrapped =
      previous !== undefined &&
      previous.length >= maxPrintLine &&
      previous.length % maxPrintLine === 0 &&
      !startsLogicalLine(raw);

    if (previousWasWrapped) {
      out[out.length - 1] = previous + raw;
    } else {
      out.push(raw);
    }
  }

  return out;
}

/** Recognises the path TeX prints after `(` when opening a file. */
const OPEN_FILE = /^[^()\s]*\.(?:tex|sty|cls|clo|cfg|def|fd|ldf|bbl|aux|toc|lof|lot|out|bst|enc|map)$/i;

/**
 * Tracks TeX's open-file stack across a log.
 *
 * TeX does not delimit these records, and parentheses occur freely in prose, so
 * exact reconstruction is impossible. This scanner only pushes when `(` is
 * followed by something that looks like a TeX input path, and tolerates
 * unbalanced `)` by ignoring pops on an empty stack — which keeps attribution
 * stable instead of desynchronising for the rest of the document.
 */
class FileStack {
  private stack: string[];
  private seen = new Set<string>();
  readonly order: string[] = [];

  constructor(root: string) {
    this.stack = [root];
    this.note(root);
  }

  private note(path: string) {
    if (!this.seen.has(path)) {
      this.seen.add(path);
      this.order.push(path);
    }
  }

  current(): string {
    return this.stack[this.stack.length - 1];
  }

  /** Applies every open/close event on one log line. */
  consume(line: string): void {
    for (let i = 0; i < line.length; i++) {
      const char = line[i];

      if (char === '(') {
        let end = i + 1;
        while (end < line.length && !'()[] '.includes(line[end])) end++;
        const candidate = line.slice(i + 1, end);
        if (OPEN_FILE.test(candidate)) {
          const path = normalisePath(candidate);
          this.stack.push(path);
          this.note(path);
          i = end - 1;
        }
      } else if (char === ')') {
        if (this.stack.length > 1) this.stack.pop();
      }
    }
  }
}

function normalisePath(path: string): string {
  return path.replace(/^\.\//, '').replace(/\\/g, '/');
}

interface Builder {
  diagnostics: CompileDiagnostic[];
  counter: number;
}

function push(
  builder: Builder,
  diagnostic: Omit<CompileDiagnostic, 'id'>,
): void {
  builder.diagnostics.push({
    id: `tex-${builder.counter++}`,
    ...diagnostic,
  });
}

/** Classifies a `! ...` error and derives an actionable hint where possible. */
function classifyError(
  message: string,
  context: string,
  sourceLine?: number,
): {
  code: DiagnosticCode;
  hint?: string;
  suggestedFix?: DiagnosticSuggestedFix;
  missingPackage?: string;
  missingFile?: string;
} {
  const notFound = message.match(/File [`'"]([^`'"]+)[`'"] not found/i);
  if (notFound) {
    const target = notFound[1];
    if (/\.sty$/i.test(target)) {
      const name = target.replace(/\.sty$/i, '');
      return {
        code: 'missing-package',
        missingPackage: name,
        hint: `Package "${name}" is not in the preloaded TeX Live set. It will be fetched on demand if the remote package endpoint is reachable.`,
        suggestedFix: {
          title: `Add \\usepackage{${name}}`,
          description: `Inserts package declaration in preamble.`,
          replacement: `\\usepackage{${name}}`,
          startLine: 1,
          endLine: 1,
        },
      };
    }
    if (/\.(?:png|jpe?g|pdf|eps|svg)$/i.test(target)) {
      return {
        code: 'missing-graphic',
        missingFile: target,
        hint: `Upload "${target}" to the project, or correct the path in \\includegraphics.`,
      };
    }
    return {
      code: 'missing-file',
      missingFile: target,
      hint: `Add "${target}" to the project, or correct the path.`,
    };
  }

  if (/^Undefined control sequence/i.test(message)) {
    // TeX may append the rest of the source line after the offending macro.
    const macro = context.match(/\\[a-zA-Z@]+/);
    const macroName = macro ? macro[0] : '';
    let suggestedFix: DiagnosticSuggestedFix | undefined;

    if (macroName === '\\includegraphics') {
      suggestedFix = {
        title: 'Add \\usepackage{graphicx}',
        description: 'Loads graphicx package required for \\includegraphics.',
        replacement: '\\usepackage{graphicx}',
        startLine: 1,
        endLine: 1,
      };
    } else if (['\\align', '\\bmatrix', '\\pmatrix', '\\eqref', '\\DeclareMathOperator', '\\substack'].includes(macroName)) {
      suggestedFix = {
        title: 'Add \\usepackage{amsmath}',
        description: 'Loads amsmath package required for advanced mathematics.',
        replacement: '\\usepackage{amsmath}',
        startLine: 1,
        endLine: 1,
      };
    } else if (['\\url', '\\href', '\\hypersetup'].includes(macroName)) {
      suggestedFix = {
        title: 'Add \\usepackage{hyperref}',
        description: 'Loads hyperref package required for hyperlinks and URLs.',
        replacement: '\\usepackage{hyperref}',
        startLine: 1,
        endLine: 1,
      };
    } else if (['\\color', '\\textcolor', '\\colorbox', '\\definecolor'].includes(macroName)) {
      suggestedFix = {
        title: 'Add \\usepackage{xcolor}',
        description: 'Loads xcolor package required for color styling.',
        replacement: '\\usepackage{xcolor}',
        startLine: 1,
        endLine: 1,
      };
    } else if (['\\toprule', '\\midrule', '\\bottomrule'].includes(macroName)) {
      suggestedFix = {
        title: 'Add \\usepackage{booktabs}',
        description: 'Loads booktabs package required for publication-quality tables.',
        replacement: '\\usepackage{booktabs}',
        startLine: 1,
        endLine: 1,
      };
    }

    return {
      code: 'undefined-control-sequence',
      hint: macro
        ? `${macro[0]} is not defined. Check the spelling, or load the package that provides it.`
        : 'A command used here is not defined. Check the spelling, or load the package that provides it.',
      suggestedFix,
    };
  }

  const unknownEnv = message.match(
    /Environment ([^\s]+) undefined|\\begin\{([^}]+)\} on input line/i,
  );
  if (unknownEnv) {
    const name = unknownEnv[1] || unknownEnv[2];
    let suggestedFix: DiagnosticSuggestedFix | undefined;
    if (name === 'tabularx') {
      suggestedFix = {
        title: 'Add \\usepackage{tabularx}',
        description: 'Loads tabularx package required for flexible width tables.',
        replacement: '\\usepackage{tabularx}',
        startLine: 1,
        endLine: 1,
      };
    } else if (name === 'algorithm' || name === 'algorithmic') {
      suggestedFix = {
        title: 'Add \\usepackage{algorithm}',
        description: 'Loads algorithm package for typesetting algorithms.',
        replacement: '\\usepackage{algorithm}',
        startLine: 1,
        endLine: 1,
      };
    } else if (name === 'listing' || name === 'lstlisting') {
      suggestedFix = {
        title: 'Add \\usepackage{listings}',
        description: 'Loads listings package for source code formatting.',
        replacement: '\\usepackage{listings}',
        startLine: 1,
        endLine: 1,
      };
    } else if (['align', 'gather', 'multline', 'equation*'].includes(name)) {
      suggestedFix = {
        title: 'Add \\usepackage{amsmath}',
        description: 'Loads amsmath package for multi-line math environments.',
        replacement: '\\usepackage{amsmath}',
        startLine: 1,
        endLine: 1,
      };
    }

    return {
      code: 'undefined-environment',
      hint: `Environment "${name}" is not defined. Load the package that provides it, or define it with \\newenvironment.`,
      suggestedFix,
    };
  }

  if (/Emergency stop|Fatal error occurred|job aborted/i.test(message)) {
    return { code: 'fatal' };
  }

  if (/perhaps a missing \\item/i.test(message)) {
    return {
      code: 'syntax',
      hint: 'A list environment is missing an \\item command before text.',
      suggestedFix: sourceLine ? {
        title: 'Insert \\item',
        description: 'Adds missing \\item to list environment.',
        replacement: '\\item ',
        startLine: sourceLine,
        endLine: sourceLine,
      } : undefined,
    };
  }

  if (
    /Missing [$}{]|Extra [}$]|Misplaced|Too many \}|Paragraph ended before|Missing \\(?:begin|end)|runaway argument/i.test(
      message,
    )
  ) {
    return { code: 'syntax' };
  }

  return { code: 'other' };
}

/**
 * Parses a pdfTeX/XeTeX/LuaTeX log into structured diagnostics.
 *
 * @param log  Raw engine log.
 * @param root Project-relative path of the compiled entry file, used as the
 *             base of the file-attribution stack.
 */
export function parseTexLog(
  log: string,
  { root = 'main.tex', maxPrintLine = DEFAULT_MAX_PRINT_LINE } = {},
): TexLogParseResult {
  const lines = unwrapLogLines(log, maxPrintLine);
  const files = new FileStack(normalisePath(root));
  const builder: Builder = { diagnostics: [], counter: 0 };

  const missingPackages = new Set<string>();
  const missingFiles = new Set<string>();
  let rerunRequired = false;
  let fatal = false;

  for (let i = 0; i < lines.length; i++) {
    const line = lines[i];

    // --- Errors: "! message", followed by context and an l.NN excerpt -------
    if (line.startsWith('! ')) {
      const message = line.slice(2).trim();
      const rawParts = [line];
      let sourceLine: number | undefined;
      let context = '';

      // TeX emits the context within a handful of lines; `l.NN` terminates it.
      for (let j = i + 1; j < Math.min(lines.length, i + 12); j++) {
        const ahead = lines[j];
        rawParts.push(ahead);

        const excerpt = ahead.match(/^l\.(\d+)\s?(.*)$/);
        if (excerpt) {
          sourceLine = Number.parseInt(excerpt[1], 10);
          context = excerpt[2];
          // The continuation line holds the text after the error point.
          if (j + 1 < lines.length && !lines[j + 1].startsWith('!')) {
            context += lines[j + 1].trimStart();
            rawParts.push(lines[j + 1]);
          }
          break;
        }
        if (ahead.startsWith('! ')) break;
      }

      const classified = classifyError(message, context, sourceLine);
      if (classified.missingPackage) missingPackages.add(classified.missingPackage);
      if (classified.missingFile) missingFiles.add(classified.missingFile);
      if (classified.code === 'fatal') fatal = true;

      push(builder, {
        severity: 'error',
        code: classified.code,
        message,
        file: files.current(),
        line: sourceLine,
        context: context.trim() || undefined,
        hint: classified.hint,
        suggestedFix: classified.suggestedFix,
        raw: rawParts.join('\n'),
      });

      files.consume(line);
      continue;
    }

    // --- "No file foo.tex." — a missing \input, which TeX only warns about --
    const noFile = line.match(/^No file ([^\s]+?)\.?$/);
    if (noFile) {
      const target = noFile[1];
      missingFiles.add(target);
      push(builder, {
        severity: 'warning',
        code: 'missing-file',
        message: `No file ${target}`,
        file: files.current(),
        hint: `TeX could not find "${target}" and skipped it. Add it to the project, or remove the reference.`,
        raw: line,
      });
      continue;
    }

    // --- LaTeX / package warnings ------------------------------------------
    const warning = line.match(
      /^(?:(LaTeX|LaTeX Font)|(?:Package|Class)\s+(\S+))\s+(?:Font\s+)?(?:Warning|Info):\s*(.*)$/,
    );
    if (warning) {
      const origin = warning[1] || warning[2] || 'LaTeX';
      let message = warning[3].trim();

      // Warnings continue on following indented lines until a blank line.
      const rawParts = [line];
      for (let j = i + 1; j < lines.length; j++) {
        const ahead = lines[j];
        if (ahead.trim() === '' || startsLogicalLine(ahead)) break;
        if (!/^\s/.test(ahead)) break;
        message += ` ${ahead.trim()}`;
        rawParts.push(ahead);
        i = j;
      }

      const onLine = message.match(/on input line (\d+)/);
      const sourceLine = onLine ? Number.parseInt(onLine[1], 10) : undefined;

      let code: DiagnosticCode = 'other';
      let hint: string | undefined;
      let suggestedFix: DiagnosticSuggestedFix | undefined;

      const isInfo = /Info:/i.test(line);

      if (/Citation [`'"]([^`'"]+)[`'"].*undefined/i.test(message)) {
        code = 'missing-citation';
        hint = 'Run BibTeX, or check that the key exists in a .bib file included via \\bibliography.';
      } else if (/Reference [`'"]([^`'"]+)[`'"].*undefined/i.test(message)) {
        code = 'missing-reference';
        hint = 'Check the \\label spelling, or recompile — references settle on the second pass.';
      } else if (/Label [`'"]([^`'"]+)[`'"] multiply defined/i.test(message)) {
        code = 'duplicate-label';
        hint = 'Two \\label commands share a key. Rename one.';
        const labelKeyMatch = message.match(/Label [`'"]([^`'"]+)[`'"] multiply defined/i);
        const dupKey = labelKeyMatch ? labelKeyMatch[1] : '';
        if (dupKey && sourceLine) {
          suggestedFix = {
            title: `Rename duplicate label '${dupKey}'`,
            description: `Renames duplicate label to '${dupKey}-duplicate'.`,
            replacement: `\\label{${dupKey}-duplicate}`,
            startLine: sourceLine,
            endLine: sourceLine,
          };
        }
      } else if (/Rerun|Label\(s\) may have changed/i.test(message)) {
        code = 'rerun-required';
        rerunRequired = true;
      } else if (/Font shape .* (?:undefined|not available)|Size substitutions with differences/i.test(message)) {
        code = 'font-substitution';
        hint = 'TeX substituted a font shape or scaled size.';
      } else if (/File [`'"]([^`'"]+)[`'"] not found/i.test(message)) {
        const targetMatch = message.match(/File [`'"]([^`'"]+)[`'"] not found/i);
        const target = targetMatch ? targetMatch[1] : '';
        if (/\.(?:png|jpe?g|pdf|eps|svg)$/i.test(target)) {
          code = 'missing-graphic';
          hint = `Upload "${target}" to the project, or correct the path in \\includegraphics.`;
        } else {
          code = 'missing-file';
          hint = `Add "${target}" to the project, or correct the path.`;
        }
      }

      // Skip non-actionable Info logs (e.g., "LaTeX Font Info:", "Package microtype Info:", "Checking defaults for...")
      if (isInfo && code === 'other') {
        continue;
      }

      const isFontSizeSub = /Size substitutions with differences/i.test(message) || /Font shape .* in size .* not available/i.test(message);

      push(builder, {
        severity: (isInfo || code === 'rerun-required' || isFontSizeSub) ? 'info' : 'warning',
        code,
        message: origin === 'LaTeX' ? message : `[${origin}] ${message}`,
        file: files.current(),
        line: sourceLine,
        hint,
        suggestedFix,
        raw: rawParts.join('\n'),
      });
      continue;
    }

    // --- Bad boxes: the honest signal that layout did not fit --------------
    const badBox = line.match(
      /^(Overfull|Underfull)\s+\\([hv])box\s+\(([^)]*)\)(?:.*?at lines (\d+)--(\d+)|.*?in paragraph at lines (\d+)--(\d+)|.*?\[(\d+)\])?/,
    );
    if (badBox) {
      const [, kind, axis, detail, a1, a2, b1, b2] = badBox;
      const startLine = a1 ?? b1;
      const endLine = a2 ?? b2;

      push(builder, {
        severity: 'warning',
        code: kind === 'Overfull' ? 'overfull-box' : 'underfull-box',
        message: `${kind} \\${axis}box (${detail})`,
        file: files.current(),
        line: startLine ? Number.parseInt(startLine, 10) : undefined,
        endLine: endLine ? Number.parseInt(endLine, 10) : undefined,
        hint:
          kind === 'Overfull'
            ? 'Content extends past the text block. Rephrase, allow hyphenation, or resize the offending box.'
            : 'TeX stretched this line or column further than it prefers. Usually cosmetic.',
        raw: line,
      });
      continue;
    }

    // --- Missing glyphs: a font genuinely lacks the requested character ----
    const missingGlyph = line.match(
      /^Missing character: There is no (.+?) \(?U?\+?([0-9A-Fa-f]*)\)? in font (.+?)!?$/,
    );
    if (missingGlyph) {
      push(builder, {
        severity: 'warning',
        code: 'missing-glyph',
        message: `Font "${missingGlyph[3]}" has no glyph for ${missingGlyph[1]}`,
        file: files.current(),
        hint: 'This character will be absent from the output. Load a font covering it, or compile with XeLaTeX/LuaLaTeX for full Unicode coverage.',
        raw: line,
      });
      continue;
    }

    if (/no output PDF file produced/i.test(line)) {
      fatal = true;
    }

    files.consume(line);
  }

  return {
    diagnostics: builder.diagnostics,
    missingPackages: [...missingPackages],
    missingFiles: [...missingFiles],
    rerunRequired,
    fatal,
    filesRead: files.order,
  };
}
````

````typescript
/**
 * Teeex Studio — Virtual TeX Filesystem & Binary Asset Synchronization
 * Provides robust base64 Data URL <-> Uint8Array buffer decoding and
 * in-memory virtual asset tree mounting for WebAssembly TeX engines and PDF pipelines.
 */

import type { ProjectFile } from '../types/latex';

const MAX_DATA_URL_CACHE = 100;
const dataUrlCache = new Map<string, Uint8Array>();

/**
 * Converts a base64 Data URL or raw base64 string to a raw Uint8Array binary buffer.
 * Strips any MIME prefix (e.g. data:image/png;base64,) and validates headers.
 */
export function dataUrlToUint8Array(dataUrl: string): Uint8Array {
  if (!dataUrl) return new Uint8Array(0);
  const cached = dataUrlCache.get(dataUrl);
  if (cached) return cached;

  const base64 = dataUrl.includes(',') ? dataUrl.split(',')[1] : dataUrl;
  try {
    const binary = atob(base64.trim());
    const bytes = new Uint8Array(binary.length);
    for (let i = 0; i < binary.length; i++) {
      bytes[i] = binary.charCodeAt(i);
    }
    if (dataUrlCache.size >= MAX_DATA_URL_CACHE) {
      const firstKey = dataUrlCache.keys().next().value;
      if (firstKey) dataUrlCache.delete(firstKey);
    }
    dataUrlCache.set(dataUrl, bytes);
    return bytes;
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('Failed to decode dataUrl to Uint8Array:', err);
    return new Uint8Array(0);
  }
}

/**
 * Converts raw Uint8Array binary bytes into a browser Data URL.
 */
export function uint8ArrayToDataUrl(bytes: Uint8Array, mimeType: string = 'image/png'): string {
  const CHUNK_SIZE = 0x8000; // 32768
  const chunks: string[] = [];
  const len = bytes.length;
  for (let i = 0; i < len; i += CHUNK_SIZE) {
    const sub = bytes.subarray(i, Math.min(i + CHUNK_SIZE, len));
    chunks.push(String.fromCharCode.apply(null, sub as unknown as number[]));
  }
  const base64 = btoa(chunks.join(''));
  return `data:${mimeType};base64,${base64}`;
}

export interface VirtualFileEntry {
  path: string;
  isBinary: boolean;
  content: string | Uint8Array;
  sizeBytes: number;
  mimeType?: string;
}

import { getPlaceholderGraphicBytes, isGraphicFilename } from './placeholderGraphics';

/**
 * Mounts and normalizes project files into an in-memory virtual filesystem map
 * ensuring all binary images/figures are converted to raw Uint8Array buffers
 * to prevent corrupted headers when compiled with WebAssembly TeX engines.
 */
export function mountVirtualTeXFileSystem(files: ProjectFile[]): Map<string, VirtualFileEntry> {
  const vfs = new Map<string, VirtualFileEntry>();

  for (const file of files) {
    const isImage = file.type === 'image' || Boolean(file.dataUrl) || isGraphicFilename(file.name);

    if (isImage) {
      let buffer: Uint8Array | null = null;
      if (file.dataUrl) {
        const decoded = dataUrlToUint8Array(file.dataUrl);
        if (decoded.byteLength > 0) buffer = decoded;
      }
      if (!buffer && file.content && typeof file.content === 'string' && file.content.startsWith('data:')) {
        const decoded = dataUrlToUint8Array(file.content);
        if (decoded.byteLength > 0) buffer = decoded;
      }
      // If buffer is missing, empty, or corrupted, provide our standard valid dummy placeholder
      if (!buffer || buffer.byteLength === 0) {
        buffer = getPlaceholderGraphicBytes(file.name);
      }

      const ext = file.name.split('.').pop()?.toLowerCase();
      const mime = ext === 'svg' ? 'image/svg+xml' : ext === 'pdf' ? 'application/pdf' : `image/${ext === 'jpg' ? 'jpeg' : ext}`;

      const entry: VirtualFileEntry = {
        path: file.name,
        isBinary: true,
        content: buffer,
        sizeBytes: buffer.byteLength,
        mimeType: mime,
      };

      // Mount under primary name
      vfs.set(file.name, entry);
      // Mount under ./ prefix
      if (!file.name.startsWith('./') && !file.name.startsWith('/')) {
        vfs.set(`./${file.name}`, entry);
      }
      // Mount under basename if different
      const basename = file.name.split('/').pop();
      if (basename && basename !== file.name) {
        vfs.set(basename, entry);
        vfs.set(`./${basename}`, entry);
      }
      // Mount under folder path if folder is specified
      if (file.folder && !file.name.startsWith(file.folder + '/')) {
        vfs.set(`${file.folder}/${file.name}`, entry);
      }
    } else {
      const entry: VirtualFileEntry = {
        path: file.name,
        isBinary: false,
        content: file.content || '',
        sizeBytes: (file.content || '').length,
        mimeType: file.name.endsWith('.bib') ? 'application/x-bibtex' : 'text/x-tex',
      };
      vfs.set(file.name, entry);
      const basename = file.name.split('/').pop();
      if (basename && basename !== file.name) {
        vfs.set(basename, entry);
      }
    }
  }

  return vfs;
}

/**
 * Resolves a file reference from LaTeX source code (e.g. \includegraphics{figures/logo} or \input{intro})
 * against the project files, handling extension omissions and path normalizations.
 */
export function resolveProjectAsset(
  referencePath: string,
  files?: ProjectFile[]
): ProjectFile | undefined {
  if (!files || files.length === 0 || !referencePath) return undefined;

  const rawClean = referencePath.trim().replace(/^[.\\/]+/, '');
  const clean = rawClean.replace(/\\/g, '/');
  const baseName = clean.split('/').pop() || clean;
  const noExtName = baseName.replace(/\.[^/.]+$/, '');
  const cleanNoExt = clean.replace(/\.[^/.]+$/, '');

  // 1. Exact match on id or name
  let matched = files.find(f => f.id === clean || f.name === clean);
  if (matched) return matched;

  // 2. Basename match
  matched = files.find(f => {
    const fBase = f.name.split('/').pop() || f.name;
    return fBase === baseName || f.id === baseName;
  });
  if (matched) return matched;

  // 3. Match without extension (e.g. \includegraphics{fig} -> fig.png)
  matched = files.find(f => {
    const fCleanNoExt = f.name.replace(/\.[^/.]+$/, '');
    const fBaseNoExt = (f.name.split('/').pop() || f.name).replace(/\.[^/.]+$/, '');
    return fCleanNoExt === cleanNoExt || fBaseNoExt === noExtName;
  });
  if (matched) return matched;

  // 4. Folder relative match
  matched = files.find(f => {
    if (f.folder && `${f.folder}/${f.name}` === clean) return true;
    if (f.folder && `${f.folder}/${f.name}`.replace(/\.[^/.]+$/, '') === cleanNoExt) return true;
    return false;
  });
  if (matched) return matched;

  // 5. Suffix or contains match for figures
  matched = files.find(f => f.name.endsWith('/' + clean) || clean.endsWith('/' + f.name));
  if (matched) return matched;

  return undefined;
}
````
